source.text: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον.

records.literal_gloss: And having risen up all the multitude of them led him to the Pilate.

en.L: And the whole multitude of them rose up and led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Pilate.
en.B: Then the whole assembly got up and brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} before Pilate.
en.R: Then the whole council got up and took Jesus to Pilate.

es.L: Y, levantándose toda la multitud de ellos, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron ante Pilato.
es.B: Entonces toda la asamblea se levantó y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó ante Pilato.
es.R: Entonces todos los del Consejo Supremo se levantaron y llevaron a Jesús ante Pilato.

fr.L: Et toute leur multitude se leva et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} conduisit devant Pilate.
fr.B: Alors toute l’assemblée se leva et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mena devant Pilate.
fr.R: Ensuite, tous les membres du conseil se sont levés et ils ont emmené Jésus chez Pilate.

sw.L: Na kundi lao lote likainuka, likampeleka kwa Pilato.
sw.B: Kisha kusanyiko lote liliinuka, likampeleka mbele ya Pilato.
sw.R: Kisha wajumbe wote wa baraza kuu waliinuka, wakampeleka Yesu kwa Pilato.

vi.L: Và cả đoàn người của họ đứng dậy, giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến Phi-lát.
vi.B: Bấy giờ cả hội đồng đứng dậy và giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến trước Phi-lát.
vi.R: Rồi cả hội đồng đứng dậy và đưa Đức Giê-xu đến Phi-lát, quan tổng đốc La Mã.

ko.L: 그리고 그들의 온 무리가 일어나서 그분을 빌라도에게로 끌고 갔다.
ko.B: 그러자 온 무리가 일어나 예수를 빌라도 앞으로 끌고 갔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 유대 최고 의회의 의원들이 모두 일어나 예수를 로마 총독 빌라도에게 끌고 갔다.

decisions.choice: the whole multitude of them: the council that had questioned Jesus
decisions.reason: "Them" points back to the elders, chief priests and scribes who met as the council at daybreak (22:66). The people and the crowds join later (23:4, 13).

decisions.choice: Pilate: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea
decisions.reason: Pilate governed Judea for the emperor (3:1), from about AD 26 to 36. The council could not carry out a death sentence on its own authority (John 18:31), so it brought Jesus to him.

decisions.choice: the whole council
decisions.reason: Readable says who the multitude was, as the context shows.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on the separate pronouns and possessives (lo, le, él, ti, tú, mí, su, tu, mi); none on pronouns joined to the verb (verlo, acusarlo, sálvate) or where Spanish leaves the subject out
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually drops the subject pronoun where English says "he", and a pronoun joined to the verb cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. As in Mark 15 and Matthew 27; this holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), with the imperfect for background and for Luke's continuing actions ("ils insistaient", "il l’interrogeait")
decisions.reason: As for the whole book (1:5): the passé simple is the tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on the verbs (likampeleka, wakamshtaki); spans on free pronouns and possessives only (yeye, wewe, mwenyewe, yake, wake, naye, nami, mimi, yangu, mwako)
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the verb's object prefix -m-, which cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter, as in Mark 15 and Matthew 27.

decisions.choice: "cả đoàn người của họ" (L); "cả hội đồng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "the whole multitude of them"; Balanced and Readable say who they were, the council that had questioned Jesus (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시- ("그분" at Literal), Jesus speaks in 해라체, Pilate, Herod's men and the mockers speak to him without honorifics, and Jesus prays to the Father in 합쇼체, through chapter 23
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (Korean style guide, sections 4 and 7); the speech levels are those of the Korean Mark 15 and John 18-19.

decisions.choice: "유대 최고 의회의 의원들" and "로마 총독 빌라도" (R)
decisions.reason: The multitude is the council (meaning decision); Readable names it and Pilate's office with the words of the Korean Mark 15:1 Readable.

source.text: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ κωλύοντα φόρους Καίσαρι διδόναι καὶ λέγοντα αὑτὸν χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι.

records.literal_gloss: They began then to accuse him saying, This [man] we found misleading the nation of us and forbidding tributes to Caesar to give and saying himself Christ a king to be.

en.L: And they began to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "We found this man misleading our nation and forbidding [us] to pay taxes to Caesar and saying that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, a king."
en.B: They started to bring charges against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "We have found this man leading our nation astray. He forbids paying taxes to Caesar, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} claims to be {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, a king."
en.R: They began to accuse Jesus. They said, "We caught this man leading our people the wrong way. He tells them not to pay taxes to Caesar. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, a king!"

es.L: Y comenzaron a acusarlo, diciendo: «Hemos encontrado a este descarriando a nuestra nación, prohibiendo pagar tributos al César y diciendo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo es {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, un rey».
es.B: Comenzaron a presentar cargos contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: «Hemos encontrado a este hombre extraviando a nuestra nación. Prohíbe pagar impuestos al César y afirma que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, un rey».
es.R: Empezaron a acusar a Jesús. Decían: «Hemos descubierto que este hombre lleva a nuestro pueblo por mal camino. Les dice que no paguen impuestos al César. ¡Y dice que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, un rey!».

fr.L: Et ils commencèrent à {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser, disant : « Nous avons trouvé cet homme égarant notre nation, empêchant de payer les impôts à César et disant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, un roi. »
fr.B: Ils se mirent à porter des accusations contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Nous avons trouvé cet homme en train d’égarer notre nation. Il interdit de payer l’impôt à César et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prétend être le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, un roi. »
fr.R: Ils ont commencé à accuser Jésus. Ils ont dit : « Nous avons surpris cet homme en train d’entraîner notre peuple sur un mauvais chemin. Il dit aux gens de ne pas payer d’impôts à César. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, un roi ! »

sw.L: Wakaanza kumshtaki, wakisema, "Tumemwona huyu akilipotosha taifa letu, na kukataza kutoa kodi kwa Kaisari, na kusema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, mfalme."
sw.B: Walianza kuleta mashtaka dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: "Tumemkuta mtu huyu akiwapotosha watu wa taifa letu. Anakataza watu kulipa kodi kwa Kaisari, na anadai kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, mfalme."
sw.R: Walianza kumshtaki Yesu. Walisema, "Tumemkamata mtu huyu akiwaongoza watu wetu njia mbaya. Anawaambia wasilipe kodi kwa Kaisari. Tena anasema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, mfalme!"

vi.L: Họ bắt đầu tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói rằng: "Chúng tôi thấy người này làm cho dân tộc chúng tôi lầm lạc, ngăn cấm nộp thuế cho Sê-sa, và nói rằng chính mình là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, một vị vua."
vi.B: Họ bắt đầu buộc tội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Chúng tôi đã bắt gặp người này xúi giục dân tộc chúng tôi đi theo đường sai. Ông ta cấm nộp thuế cho Sê-sa, và tự xưng là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, là vua."
vi.R: Họ bắt đầu tố cáo Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói: "Chúng tôi bắt được người này đang dẫn dân chúng tôi đi sai đường. Ông ta bảo dân đừng nộp thuế cho Sê-sa. Ông ta còn nói mình là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, là vua nữa!"

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그분을 고발하기 시작하며 말했다. "우리는 이 사람이 우리 민족을 그릇된 길로 이끌고, 가이사에게 세금 바치는 것을 금하고, 자기가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}, 곧 왕이라고 말하는 것을 보았습니다."
ko.B: 그들은 예수를 고발하기 시작했다. "우리가 보니 이 사람은 우리 민족을 그릇된 길로 이끌고 있습니다. 가이사에게 세금을 바치지 못하게 하고, 자기가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}, 곧 왕이라고 주장합니다."
ko.R: 그들은 예수를 고발하기 시작했다. 그들이 말했다. "이 사람이 우리 백성을 잘못된 길로 이끄는 것을 우리가 직접 보았습니다. 이 사람은 로마 황제 가이사에게 세금을 내지 말라고 합니다. 그리고 자기가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}, 곧 왕이라고 합니다!"

decisions.choice: misleading: turning people aside, leading them astray
alternatives: teaching wrongly about the law only
decisions.reason: The verb means to twist or turn aside. Before a Roman governor it suggests stirring up the nation against Rome; the charge comes back in other words in 23:5 and 23:14.

decisions.choice: forbidding taxes to Caesar: a false charge
alternatives: a true report of Jesus' teaching
decisions.reason: When he was asked about the tax, Jesus had said to give Caesar what belongs to Caesar (20:22-25). Luke lets the reader see that the charge twists his words.

decisions.choice: Christ, a king: the Jewish title explained as a political claim
alternatives: Christ as a religious title only
decisions.reason: The accusers add "a king" to the title Christ, the anointed King of Israel (9:20), so that Pilate hears a claim to rule in Caesar's place. To Rome that was rebellion.

decisions.choice: himself: he claims it for himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun is reflexive: the charge is that Jesus makes the claim about himself.

decisions.choice: taxes
decisions.reason: The word is for the tax a subject people paid to Rome. "Tribute" is less familiar.

decisions.choice: Christ as the default, Messiah as the alternative
decisions.reason: The title follows the christos setting, as everywhere else.

decisions.choice: "người này", "ông ta" and the reflexive "mình" in the accusers' mouths, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:31: opponents speak of Jesus plainly, and neither "ông ta" nor the reflexive "mình" has a reverent capital form, so the English spans on "he himself" have no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "Sê-sa"
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration for Caesar, as the style guide lists it.

decisions.choice: The accusers speak to Pilate in 합쇼체 ("보았습니다"); the crowd shouts its demands in 하오체 (23:18, 23:21); Pilate answers in 해라체
decisions.reason: Officials making a formal charge before the governor speak up to him; the shouted demands keep the firm 하오체 and Pilate's replies the plain style of the Korean Mark 15:9-14.

decisions.choice: "가이사" (L, B), "로마 황제 가이사" (R); "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}, 곧 왕"
decisions.reason: "가이사" is the Protestant form of the style guide; Readable says who he was. "곧" sets the king beside the title, as the meaning decision explains it as a political claim; the particle after the span fits both forms.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: The but Pilate questioned him saying, You are the king of the Jews?

en.L: And Pilate questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the king of the Jews?"
en.B: So Pilate asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the king of the Jews?"
en.R: Pilate asked Jesus, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the king of the Jews?"

es.L: Y Pilato {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} interrogó, diciendo: «¿Tú eres el Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Entonces Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el Rey de los judíos?».
es.R: Pilato le preguntó a Jesús: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el rey de los judíos?».

fr.L: Et Pilate {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogea, disant : « Toi, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.B: Pilate {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogea donc : « Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.R: Pilate a demandé à Jésus : « Est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le roi des Juifs ? »

sw.L: Naye Pilato akamwuliza, akisema, "Wewe ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Basi Pilato alimwuliza, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Pilato alimwuliza Yesu, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mfalme wa Wayahudi?"

vi.L: Và Phi-lát hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói: "Anh là Vua của người Do Thái sao?"
vi.B: Phi-lát hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Anh là Vua dân Do Thái sao?"
vi.R: Phi-lát hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Anh có phải là vua của dân Do Thái không?"

ko.L: 그러자 빌라도가 그분께 물으며 말했다. "네가 유대인의 왕이냐?"
ko.B: 빌라도가 예수께 물었다. "네가 유대인의 왕이냐?"
ko.R: 빌라도가 예수께 물었다. "네가 유대인의 왕이냐?"

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, set first in the question
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first and is not needed for the sense. Pilate may be surprised that the man before him is said to be a king.

decisions.choice: the king of the Jews: the title as a Gentile would put it
decisions.reason: Jews spoke of "the king of Israel" (Mark 15:32); "king of the Jews" is how outsiders put it (Matthew 2:2). For Rome, anyone who called himself king without Caesar's leave was a rebel.

decisions.choice: el Rey de los judíos (L, B); el rey de los judíos (R); «¿Tú eres ...?» at Literal, as the Greek puts the stressed "you" first
alternatives: el rey de los judíos (every level, as the English)
decisions.reason: The Spanish drafts of Matthew 27:11 and Mark 15:2 write the title with a capital at Literal and Balanced, since Pilate asks about a royal title (meaning decision m2); Readable writes it plainly, as there. At the head of the Literal question "Tú" is capitalised either way and takes no span (meaning decision m1). The same in 23:37 and 23:38.

decisions.choice: le roi des Juifs, lowercase "roi", at every level; Pilate says "tu" to Jesus; Literal keeps the emphatic "Toi" first
decisions.reason: French writes a title such as this with a lowercase "roi", as Mark 15:2 does; the phrase stays the same in 23:37-38 so that the charge, the mockery and the notice on the cross match. The emphatic pronoun (m1) can stand first in French as "Toi, tu es ...", which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: Mfalme wa Wayahudi (L, B), mfalme wa Wayahudi (R); "ndiwe" (you are the one) at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 27:11 and Mark 15:2: the title takes a capital at Literal and Balanced, plainly at Readable, and "ndiwe" carries the stress the Greek puts on "you" (meaning decision m1). At the head of the Literal question "Wewe" is capitalised either way and takes no span. The same in 23:37 and 23:38.

decisions.choice: Pilate to Jesus: "anh", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:2 and Matthew 27:11: a governor questioning a prisoner speaks down to him but not crudely; "anh" has no capital form for the setting.

decisions.choice: Pilate speaks to Jesus in the plain style ("네가 ... 왕이냐?")
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 15:2 and John 18:33: the governor questions a prisoner; "네가" in front carries the stressed "you".

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.

records.literal_gloss: The and answering him he said, You say.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered him and said, "You say [so]."
en.B: He answered him, "You say so."
en.R: Jesus answered, "You are the one who says it."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiéndole, dijo: «Tú [lo] dices».
es.B: Él le respondió: «Tú lo dices».
es.R: Jesús le contestó: «Eres tú quien lo dice».

fr.L: Et, lui répondant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} déclara : « Tu [le] dis. »
fr.B: Il lui répondit : « C’est toi qui le dis. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « C’est toi qui dis cela. »

sw.L: Naye, akimjibu, alisema, "Wewe unasema [hivyo]."
sw.B: Alimjibu, "Wewe unasema hivyo."
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Wewe ndiye unayesema hivyo."

vi.L: Ngài trả lời ông và nói: "Ông nói [vậy]."
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Chính ông đã nói vậy."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Đó là lời của ông."

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그에게 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "네가 말한다."
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "그것은 네가 한 말이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "그것은 네 입으로 한 말이다."

decisions.choice: You say so: a reply that does not deny the title but leaves the words with Pilate
alternatives: a denial: that is your word, not mine
decisions.reason: Jesus gave the council a similar answer (22:70), and they took it as a yes (22:71). Here he does not reject the title, but he does not take it up in Pilate's sense either; Pilate goes on to find no guilt in him (23:4), so he did not hear it as a confession of rebellion.

decisions.choice: You are the one who says it
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the reserve of the answer rather than turning it into a plain yes or no.

decisions.choice: Jesus to Pilate: "ông"
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:2: courteous without deference; the words are left with Pilate (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "네가 말한다" (L); "그것은 네가 한 말이다" (B); "그것은 네 입으로 한 말이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is the same as Mark 15:2, so the Korean is the same; the reply leaves the title in Pilate's mouth without denying it (meaning decision).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους· Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, Nothing I find guilt in the man this.

en.L: And Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no guilt in this man."
en.B: Pilate told the chief priests and the crowds, "I find this man guilty of nothing."
en.R: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I do not see that this man has done anything wrong."

es.L: Y Pilato dijo a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a las multitudes: «Ninguna culpa encuentro en este hombre».
es.B: Pilato les dijo a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a las multitudes: «No encuentro a este hombre culpable de nada».
es.R: Entonces Pilato les dijo a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a la gente: «Yo no veo que este hombre haya hecho nada malo».

fr.L: Et Pilate dit aux chefs des prêtres et aux foules : « Je ne trouve en cet homme aucun motif de condamnation. »
fr.B: Pilate déclara aux chefs des prêtres et aux foules : « Je ne trouve cet homme coupable de rien. »
fr.R: Alors Pilate a dit aux chefs des prêtres et à la foule : « Je ne vois pas ce que cet homme a fait de mal. »

sw.L: Naye Pilato akawaambia wakuu wa makuhani na makundi ya watu, "Sioni hatia yoyote katika mtu huyu."
sw.B: Pilato aliwaambia wakuu wa makuhani na makundi ya watu, "Simwoni mtu huyu kuwa na hatia ya jambo lolote."
sw.R: Kisha Pilato aliwaambia wakuu wa makuhani na watu wote, "Sioni kwamba mtu huyu amefanya kosa lolote."

vi.L: Và Phi-lát nói với các thầy tế lễ cả và các đám đông: "Tôi không tìm thấy tội gì nơi người này."
vi.B: Phi-lát nói với các thầy tế lễ cả và đám đông: "Tôi không thấy người này phạm tội gì cả."
vi.R: Rồi Phi-lát nói với các thầy tế lễ cả và đám đông: "Tôi không thấy người này đã làm điều gì sai."

ko.L: 그러자 빌라도가 대제사장들과 무리에게 말했다. "나는 이 사람에게서 아무 죄도 찾지 못한다."
ko.B: 빌라도가 대제사장들과 무리에게 말했다. "나는 이 사람에게서 아무 죄목도 찾지 못하겠다."
ko.R: 그러자 빌라도가 대제사장들과 무리에게 말했다. "내가 보기에 이 사람은 아무 잘못도 하지 않았다."

decisions.choice: guilt: ground for a charge in law
decisions.reason: The word is a legal one: the cause or ground for which a person can be charged and punished. Pilate finds nothing to convict Jesus of.

decisions.choice: the first of three times Pilate declares Jesus innocent
decisions.reason: Pilate says it again in 23:14-15 and a third time in 23:22. Luke shows that the Roman judge did not find Jesus guilty of the charges (Acts 13:28).

decisions.choice: the crowds: people now gathered at Pilate's court
decisions.reason: Crowds appear for the first time in the trial. Until now the people had listened to Jesus gladly (19:48; 21:38).

decisions.choice: I find this man guilty of nothing (B); I do not see that he has done anything wrong (R)
alternatives: I find no guilt in this man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the verdict in plain words.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes (every level)
decisions.reason: The term used for this group across the New Testament drafts, as in Mark 15:1 and Matthew 27:1, recorded once in this chapter. The same in 23:10, 13 and 23.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres, at every level
decisions.reason: The New Testament term sheet: "les chefs des prêtres" for the leading priests, as in Mark 15, with "le grand prêtre" kept for the one high priest.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani (every level)
decisions.reason: The term used for this group across the New Testament drafts, as in Mark 15:1 and Matthew 27:1, recorded once in this chapter. The same in 23:10, 13 and 23.

decisions.choice: Pilate says "tôi" for himself to the leaders and the crowds
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:9: the governor keeps his distance with plain "tôi", neither humble nor archaic.

decisions.choice: "죄" (L); "죄목" (B); "잘못" (R) for aition
decisions.reason: The word is a ground for a charge in law (meaning decision); "죄목" names that, and Readable says it plainly.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε.

records.literal_gloss: They but kept insisting saying that He stirs up the people teaching throughout all the Judea, and having begun from the Galilee even to here.

en.L: But they kept insisting, saying, "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, and having begun from Galilee even to here."
en.B: But they pressed the charge harder: "He is stirring up the people with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching all over Judea. He started in Galilee and has come all the way here."
en.R: But they kept on saying, "He is getting the people all stirred up by what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} teaches. He has done it everywhere in Judea. He started in Galilee, and now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has come here!"

es.L: Pero ellos insistían, diciendo: «Alborota al pueblo, enseñando por toda Judea, y comenzando desde Galilea hasta aquí».
es.B: Pero ellos insistían con más fuerza: «Con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza alborota al pueblo por toda Judea. Comenzó en Galilea y ha llegado hasta aquí».
es.R: Pero ellos seguían diciendo: «Con lo que enseña tiene al pueblo muy alborotado. Lo ha hecho por toda Judea. ¡Comenzó en Galilea y ahora ha venido hasta aquí!».

fr.L: Mais ils insistaient, disant : « Il soulève le peuple, enseignant à travers toute la Judée, et ayant commencé depuis la Galilée jusqu’ici. »
fr.B: Mais ils redoublèrent d’insistance : « Il soulève le peuple par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} enseignement dans toute la Judée. Il a commencé en Galilée et est venu jusqu’ici. »
fr.R: Mais ils continuaient à dire : « Il agite tout le peuple avec ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseigne. Il l’a fait partout en Judée. Il a commencé en Galilée, et maintenant {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est venu jusqu’ici ! »

sw.L: Lakini wao wakazidi kusisitiza, wakisema, "Anawachochea watu, akifundisha katika Uyahudi wote, akianzia Galilaya hadi hapa."
sw.B: Lakini wao walizidi kukaza mashtaka yao: "Anawachochea watu kwa mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika Uyahudi kote. Alianzia Galilaya, na sasa amefika mpaka hapa."
sw.R: Lakini waliendelea kusema, "Anawachochea watu kwa mambo anayofundisha. Amefanya hivyo kila mahali katika Uyahudi. Alianzia Galilaya, na sasa amekuja mpaka hapa!"

vi.L: Nhưng họ càng nài ép mà nói: "Ông ta xúi giục dân chúng, giảng dạy khắp cả xứ Giu-đê, bắt đầu từ Ga-li-lê cho đến tận đây."
vi.B: Nhưng họ càng nói quyết liệt hơn: "Ông ta dùng lời giảng dạy của mình mà khuấy động dân chúng khắp xứ Giu-đê. Ông ta bắt đầu từ Ga-li-lê và nay đã đến tận đây."
vi.R: Nhưng họ cứ nói mãi: "Những điều ông ta dạy làm cho dân chúng nổi loạn. Ông ta đã làm như vậy khắp xứ Giu-đê. Ông ta bắt đầu từ Ga-li-lê, và bây giờ đã đến tận đây!"

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 더욱 우기며 말했다. "그는 온 유대에 두루 가르치면서 백성을 선동합니다. 갈릴리에서부터 시작하여 여기까지 [왔습니다]."
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 더욱 거세게 주장했다. "그는 온 유대를 다니며 가르쳐서 백성을 선동하고 있습니다. 갈릴리에서 시작해서 이곳까지 왔습니다."
ko.R: 그러나 그들은 계속 우겼다. "이 사람은 가르치는 것으로 백성을 들쑤셔 놓고 있습니다. 유대 온 땅에서 그렇게 했습니다. 갈릴리에서 시작해서 이제 여기까지 왔습니다!"

decisions.choice: stirs up: incites, shakes the people into unrest
decisions.reason: The verb pictures shaking something violently; it is used for stirring a crowd to riot. The charge is no longer only about words but about disorder.

decisions.choice: Judea: the whole land of the Jews
alternatives: the Roman province of Judea only
decisions.reason: Luke sometimes uses Judea for the whole country, Galilee included (4:44; 7:17). Peter sums up Jesus' ministry in the same way, "throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee" (Acts 10:37).

decisions.choice: having begun from Galilee: the word Galilee leads into the next scene
decisions.reason: The mention of Galilee prompts Pilate's question in 23:6.

decisions.choice: pressed the charge harder
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow stronger or to insist more. Balanced says what they were insisting on.

decisions.choice: Uyahudi (every level)
decisions.reason: The Swahili name for Judea used in John and across these drafts. Here it means the whole land of the Jews (meaning decision m2), which "Uyahudi" covers naturally.

decisions.choice: Galilee in the last sentence at every level; [왔습니다] supplied (L)
alternatives: one sentence ending on the verb "선동합니다"
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last; a separate last sentence keeps "Galilee" where the Greek has it, leading into 23:6 (meaning decision). The Greek phrase has no verb, which Literal brackets.

source.text: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν, καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην, ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

records.literal_gloss: Pilate now having heard asked whether the man a Galilean is, \v 7 and having learned that from the jurisdiction of Herod he is he sent up him to Herod, being also himself in Jerusalem in these the days.

en.L: And when Pilate heard [this], he asked whether the man was a Galilean, \v 7 and having learned that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was from Herod's jurisdiction, he sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up to Herod, who was himself also in Jerusalem in those days.
en.B: When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was from Galilee. \v 7 When he learned that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came under Herod's authority, he sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem at that time.
en.R: When Pilate heard this, he asked if Jesus came from Galilee. \v 7 He found out that Jesus was from the area that Herod ruled. So he sent Jesus to Herod. Herod was in Jerusalem at that time too.

es.L: Y Pilato, al oír [esto], preguntó si el hombre era galileo, \v 7 y, al saber que era de la jurisdicción de Herodes, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} remitió a Herodes, que también estaba en Jerusalén en aquellos días.
es.B: Al oír esto, Pilato preguntó si aquel hombre era de Galilea. \v 7 Cuando supo que estaba bajo la autoridad de Herodes, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envió a Herodes, que también se encontraba en Jerusalén en esos días.
es.R: Cuando Pilato oyó esto, preguntó si Jesús era de Galilea. \v 7 Supo que Jesús era de la región que gobernaba Herodes. Así que mandó a Jesús adonde estaba Herodes. Herodes también estaba en Jerusalén en esos días.

fr.L: Et Pilate, ayant entendu [cela], demanda si l’homme était galiléen, \v 7 et ayant appris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était de la juridiction d’Hérode, il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} renvoya devant Hérode, qui était lui aussi à Jérusalem en ces jours-là.
fr.B: Quand Pilate entendit cela, il demanda si cet homme était galiléen. \v 7 Ayant appris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} relevait de l’autorité d’Hérode, il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} renvoya devant Hérode, qui se trouvait lui aussi à Jérusalem en ces jours-là.
fr.R: Quand Pilate a entendu cela, il a demandé si Jésus venait de Galilée. \v 7 Il a appris que Jésus venait de la région que gouvernait Hérode. Alors il a envoyé Jésus à Hérode. Hérode aussi était à Jérusalem à ce moment-là.

sw.L: Naye Pilato aliposikia [hayo], aliuliza kama mtu huyo ni Mgalilaya, \v 7 na alipojua kwamba yuko chini ya mamlaka ya Herode, alimpeleka kwa Herode, ambaye yeye pia alikuwa Yerusalemu siku hizo.
sw.B: Pilato aliposikia hayo, aliuliza kama mtu huyo alikuwa wa Galilaya. \v 7 Alipojua kwamba yuko chini ya mamlaka ya Herode, akampeleka kwa Herode, ambaye naye alikuwa Yerusalemu wakati huo.
sw.R: Pilato aliposikia hivyo, aliuliza kama Yesu alitoka Galilaya. \v 7 Akagundua kwamba Yesu alitoka katika eneo lililotawaliwa na Herode. Kwa hiyo akampeleka Yesu kwa Herode. Herode naye alikuwa Yerusalemu wakati huo.

vi.L: Nghe [vậy], Phi-lát hỏi xem người này có phải là người Ga-li-lê không, \v 7 và khi biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thuộc quyền cai trị của Hê-rốt, ông giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên Hê-rốt, là người cũng đang ở Giê-ru-sa-lem trong những ngày ấy.
vi.B: Nghe vậy, Phi-lát hỏi người này có phải là người Ga-li-lê không. \v 7 Khi biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thuộc quyền cai trị của Hê-rốt, ông chuyển {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sang cho Hê-rốt, vì lúc ấy Hê-rốt cũng đang ở Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Nghe vậy, Phi-lát hỏi xem Đức Giê-xu có phải từ Ga-li-lê đến không. \v 7 Ông biết được rằng Đức Giê-xu đến từ miền do Hê-rốt cai trị. Vì vậy ông gửi Đức Giê-xu sang cho Hê-rốt. Lúc ấy Hê-rốt cũng đang ở Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그런데 빌라도가 [이 말을] 듣고 그 사람이 갈릴리 사람이냐고 물었다. \v 7 그리고 그분이 헤롯의 관할 아래 있는 것을 알고, 그분을 헤롯에게 보냈다. 헤롯 자신도 그 무렵에 예루살렘에 있었다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 이 말을 듣고, 그 사람이 갈릴리 사람이냐고 물었다. \v 7 그리고 예수께서 헤롯의 관할에 속한 것을 알고, 예수를 헤롯에게 보냈다. 그때 헤롯도 예루살렘에 와 있었다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 이 말을 듣고, 예수께서 갈릴리 출신인지 물었다. \v 7 그리고 예수께서 헤롯이 다스리는 지역에서 오신 것을 알게 되었다. 그래서 빌라도는 예수를 헤롯에게 보냈다. 헤롯도 그때 예루살렘에 와 있었다.

decisions.choice: Herod: Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: This is the son of Herod the Great, who ruled Galilee and Perea for Rome (3:1). He had John the Baptist beheaded (9:9), and Pharisees once warned that he wanted to kill Jesus (13:31).

decisions.choice: jurisdiction: the area under his authority
decisions.reason: The word for authority here means the territory over which a ruler has the right to judge.

decisions.choice: sent up: referred the case to another authority
decisions.reason: The verb was used for sending a case on to another court. It is used again when Herod sends Jesus back (23:11, 15).

decisions.choice: Herod was in Jerusalem: for the Passover
decisions.reason: Herod's capital was in Galilee; he had come to Jerusalem for the feast (22:1).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, since Pilate, Herod and Jesus all appear in the sentence.

decisions.choice: renvoya devant Hérode
decisions.reason: The verb is the term for referring a case to another authority (m3); French "renvoyer devant" is the legal phrase for sending a case to another court. The same verb in 23:11 and 23:15 is "renvoyer", there in the sense of sending back.

decisions.choice: "giải ... lên" (L); "chuyển ... sang" (B); "gửi ... sang" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is used of referring a case to another authority (meaning decision); Literal keeps "up", the other levels say the case was passed on. Herod is "Hê-rốt" as in Luke 3:1.

decisions.choice: "관할" (L, B); "헤롯이 다스리는 지역" (R) for exousia
decisions.reason: The word here is the area under Herod's authority (meaning decision); "관할" is the Korean legal word, and Readable says it plainly.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν, ἦν γὰρ ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον.

records.literal_gloss: The and Herod having seen the Jesus was glad exceedingly, he was for of long times wishing to see him because of the hearing about him, and he was hoping some sign to see by him done.

en.L: And when Herod saw Jesus, he was very glad, for he had been wanting to see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a long time because he had been hearing about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and he was hoping to see some sign done by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Herod was delighted when he saw Jesus. He had wanted to see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a long time because of what he had heard about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and he hoped to watch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} perform some sign.
en.R: Herod was very happy to see Jesus. He had heard about Jesus and had wanted to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a long time. He hoped Jesus would do some sign, a miracle, while he watched.

es.L: Y Herodes, al ver a Jesús, se alegró mucho, porque desde hacía bastante tiempo quería verlo, por lo que oía acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y esperaba ver alguna señal hecha por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Herodes se alegró muchísimo al ver a Jesús. Hacía mucho tiempo que quería verlo por lo que había oído de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y esperaba verlo hacer alguna señal.
es.R: Herodes se puso muy contento al ver a Jesús. Había oído hablar de Jesús y hacía mucho tiempo que quería conocerlo. Esperaba que Jesús hiciera alguna señal, algún milagro, delante de él.

fr.L: Et Hérode, voyant Jésus, se réjouit beaucoup, car depuis longtemps il désirait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir, parce qu’il entendait [parler] de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et il espérait voir quelque signe accompli par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Hérode fut très heureux de voir Jésus. Il désirait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir depuis longtemps, à cause de ce qu’il avait entendu dire de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et il espérait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} voir accomplir quelque signe.
fr.R: Hérode a été très content de voir Jésus. Il avait entendu parler de Jésus, et il voulait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rencontrer depuis longtemps. Il espérait que Jésus ferait un signe, un miracle, devant lui.

sw.L: Naye Herode alipomwona Yesu, alifurahi sana, kwa kuwa kwa muda mrefu alikuwa akitaka kumwona kwa sababu ya kusikia habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, tena alikuwa akitumaini kuona ishara fulani ikifanywa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Herode alipomwona Yesu alifurahi mno. Kwa muda mrefu alikuwa ametaka kumwona kwa sababu ya habari alizosikia juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, naye alitumaini kumwona akifanya ishara fulani.
sw.R: Herode alifurahi sana kumwona Yesu. Alikuwa amesikia habari za Yesu, na kwa muda mrefu alikuwa ametaka kukutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Alitumaini kwamba Yesu angefanya ishara fulani, yaani muujiza, mbele yake.

vi.L: Còn Hê-rốt, khi thấy Đức Giê-xu thì rất vui mừng, vì từ lâu ông đã muốn gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, bởi đã nghe nói về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và ông hy vọng được thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm một dấu lạ nào đó.
vi.B: Hê-rốt rất mừng khi thấy Đức Giê-xu. Từ lâu ông đã muốn gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì ông đã nghe nhiều về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và ông mong được xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm một dấu lạ nào đó.
vi.R: Hê-rốt rất vui khi gặp Đức Giê-xu. Ông đã nghe nói về Đức Giê-xu, và từ lâu ông đã muốn gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ông mong Đức Giê-xu sẽ làm một dấu lạ nào đó cho ông xem.

ko.L: 헤롯은 예수를 보고 매우 기뻐했다. 그분에 관하여 들어 왔기 때문에 오래전부터 그분을 보고 싶어 하고 있었고, 그분이 어떤 표적을 행하시는 것을 보기를 바라고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 헤롯은 예수를 보고 몹시 기뻐했다. 예수에 관한 소문을 들어서 오래전부터 만나 보고 싶어 했기 때문이다. 그리고 예수께서 어떤 표적을 행하시는 것을 직접 보기를 바랐다.
ko.R: 헤롯은 예수를 보고 무척 기뻤다. 헤롯은 예수에 대해 많이 들었고, 오래전부터 예수를 만나고 싶어 했다. 그는 예수께서 어떤 표적, 곧 놀라운 일을 일으키시는 것을 보고 싶었다.

decisions.choice: he had long wanted to see him: as Luke said in 9:9
decisions.reason: When Herod heard of Jesus' works, he asked who this was and tried to see him (9:7-9).

decisions.choice: sign: a miracle that would prove who Jesus was
decisions.reason: Herod wants a display. Jesus had refused to give signs to those who demanded them (11:16, 29).

decisions.choice: he was hoping: a continuing hope
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes a hope he had held for some time.

decisions.choice: some sign, a miracle
decisions.reason: Readable explains what kind of sign Herod wanted.

decisions.choice: un signe, un miracle (R); un signe (L, B)
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "signe" and never replaces it with "miracle"; Readable keeps the word and adds "un miracle" only as an explanation, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "dấu lạ" at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for sign, as in John 2:11 and the Vietnamese Mark 16:17; Readable does not add "phép lạ", since the style guide keeps the two apart.

decisions.choice: "표적" at every level; Readable adds "놀라운 일"
decisions.reason: "표적" is the key term of the Korean John and Mark, never "기적"; Readable explains it in plain words rather than with the English Readable's "miracle".

source.text: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς· αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: He kept questioning then him in words many; he but nothing answered him.

en.L: And he questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at length, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered him nothing.
en.B: He put question after question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but Jesus gave him no answer at all.
en.R: Herod asked Jesus many questions. But Jesus did not answer him at all.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} interrogaba con muchas palabras, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nada le respondió.
es.B: Le hacía una pregunta tras otra, pero Jesús no le respondió nada.
es.R: Herodes le hizo muchas preguntas a Jesús. Pero Jesús no le contestó nada.

fr.L: Et il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogeait longuement, mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ne lui répondit rien.
fr.B: Il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} posa question sur question, mais Jésus ne lui fit aucune réponse.
fr.R: Hérode a posé beaucoup de questions à Jésus. Mais Jésus ne lui a pas répondu du tout.

sw.L: Akawa akimwuliza kwa maneno mengi; lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakumjibu chochote.
sw.B: Alimwuliza swali baada ya swali, lakini Yesu hakumjibu hata neno moja.
sw.R: Herode alimwuliza Yesu maswali mengi. Lakini Yesu hakumjibu kabisa.

vi.L: Ông hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhiều lời, nhưng chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng trả lời ông điều gì.
vi.B: Ông hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hết câu này đến câu khác, nhưng Đức Giê-xu không trả lời ông một lời nào.
vi.R: Hê-rốt hỏi Đức Giê-xu nhiều câu. Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không trả lời ông gì cả.

ko.L: 그래서 그는 여러 말로 그분께 계속 물었으나, 그분은 그에게 아무것도 대답하지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 헤롯이 이것저것 많이 물었으나, 예수께서는 그에게 한마디도 대답하지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 헤롯은 예수께 많은 질문을 했다. 그러나 예수께서는 아무 대답도 하지 않으셨다.

decisions.choice: he answered him nothing: the silent servant
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:7 speaks of the servant who did not open his mouth, like a sheep before its shearers; Acts 8:32-35 applies that passage to Jesus.

decisions.choice: he: emphatic, in contrast to Herod
decisions.reason: The pronoun is set against Herod's many words: Herod talks, but Jesus says nothing.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since both men are "he".

source.text: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Had been standing now the chief priests and the scribes vehemently accusing him.

en.L: And the chief priests and the scribes stood [there], vehemently accusing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The chief priests and the scribes stood by, accusing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} fiercely.
en.R: The chief priests and the teachers of the law were standing there. They kept making strong charges against Jesus.

es.L: Y estaban [allí] los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas, acusándolo con vehemencia.
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas estaban allí, acusándolo con ferocidad.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley estaban allí. No dejaban de acusar a Jesús con mucha fuerza.

fr.L: Et les chefs des prêtres et les scribes se tenaient [là], {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accusant avec véhémence.
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres et les scribes étaient là et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accusaient violemment.
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres et les spécialistes de la Loi étaient là. Ils n’arrêtaient pas de lancer de graves accusations contre Jésus.

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walikuwa wamesimama [hapo], wakimshtaki kwa nguvu.
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walisimama pale, wakimshtaki vikali.
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria walikuwa wamesimama pale. Waliendelea kuleta mashtaka makali dhidi ya Yesu.

vi.L: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo đứng [đó], kịch liệt tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo đứng đó, ra sức tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy dạy luật đứng đó. Họ cứ tố cáo Đức Giê-xu thật gay gắt.

ko.L: 그리고 대제사장들과 율법학자들이 서서 맹렬하게 그분을 고발하고 있었다.
ko.B: 대제사장들과 율법학자들은 곁에 서서 예수를 격렬하게 고발했다.
ko.R: 대제사장들과 율법을 가르치는 선생들도 거기 서 있었다. 그들은 계속해서 예수를 심하게 고발했다.

decisions.choice: vehemently: with force and intensity
decisions.reason: The adverb describes doing something with all one's strength. Acts 18:28 uses it for Apollos refuting opponents.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable says what scribes were, as elsewhere in Luke.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, recorded once in this chapter. Readable says what these men were, as the English "teachers of the law" does.

decisions.choice: les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
alternatives: les maîtres de la Loi at every level
decisions.reason: The New Testament term sheet, as in Luke 6:7: Readable explains the scribes' role, as the English "teachers of the law" does.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, recorded once in this chapter. Readable says what these men were, as the English "teachers of the law" does.

decisions.choice: "các thầy tế lễ cả" (L, B, R); "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B), "các thầy dạy luật" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Gospel terms, as in the Vietnamese Mark 15:1 and 15:31.

decisions.choice: "대제사장들" at every level; "율법학자들" (L, B), "율법을 가르치는 선생들" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms settled for the Korean Gospels, as in Mark 15:1 and Luke 9:22.

source.text: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Having treated as nothing then him also the Herod with the troops of him and having mocked, having put around [him] clothing bright he sent back him to the Pilate.

en.L: And Herod with his soldiers treated {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with contempt and mocked [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], and having put bright clothing on [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], he sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to Pilate.
en.B: Herod and his soldiers treated {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with scorn and made fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Herod had {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} dressed in a bright robe and sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to Pilate.
en.R: Then Herod and his soldiers laughed at Jesus and treated {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were worth nothing. They put a shining robe on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a king. Then Herod sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to Pilate.

es.L: Y Herodes con sus tropas, después de despreciarlo y burlarse [de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}], {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} puso una ropa resplandeciente y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} devolvió a Pilato.
es.B: Herodes y sus soldados {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} trataron con desprecio y se burlaron de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Herodes {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hizo vestir con un manto espléndido y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} devolvió a Pilato.
es.R: Entonces Herodes y sus soldados se rieron de Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} trataron como si no valiera nada. Le pusieron un manto brillante, como si fuera un rey. Luego Herodes {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} mandó de vuelta a Pilato.

fr.L: Et Hérode, avec ses troupes, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traita avec mépris et, s’étant moqué [de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant revêtu d’un vêtement éclatant, il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} renvoya à Pilate.
fr.B: Hérode et ses soldats {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traitèrent avec mépris et se moquèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Hérode {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fit revêtir d’un habit éclatant et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} renvoya à Pilate.
fr.R: Ensuite, Hérode et ses soldats se sont moqués de Jésus. Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont traité comme s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne valait rien. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont mis un vêtement brillant, comme s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était un roi. Puis Hérode {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a renvoyé à Pilate.

sw.L: Na Herode pamoja na askari wake, akiisha kumdharau na kumdhihaki, akamvika vazi linalong'aa, akamrudisha kwa Pilato.
sw.B: Herode na askari wake walimdharau na kumfanyia mzaha. Herode akaagiza avikwe joho linalong'aa, kisha akamrudisha kwa Pilato.
sw.R: Kisha Herode na askari wake walimcheka Yesu, wakamtendea kana kwamba hana thamani yoyote. Wakamvika joho linalong'aa, kana kwamba ni mfalme. Kisha Herode akamrudisha kwa Pilato.

vi.L: Còn Hê-rốt cùng với các binh lính của ông khinh miệt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và chế nhạo [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}], rồi khoác cho [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] một áo rực rỡ, ông giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lại cho Phi-lát.
vi.B: Hê-rốt và quân lính của ông khinh bỉ và chế giễu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Hê-rốt cho khoác lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng lộng lẫy, rồi gửi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lại cho Phi-lát.
vi.R: Rồi Hê-rốt và lính của ông cười nhạo Đức Giê-xu và đối xử với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như một người chẳng ra gì. Họ khoác lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng sáng chói, như thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là vua. Rồi Hê-rốt gửi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lại cho Phi-lát.

ko.L: 그리고 헤롯도 자기 병사들과 함께 그분을 업신여기고 조롱하고 나서, [그분께] 빛나는 옷을 입혀 그분을 빌라도에게 돌려보냈다.
ko.B: 헤롯은 자기 병사들과 함께 예수를 업신여기며 조롱했다. 그리고 예수께 화려한 옷을 입혀 빌라도에게 돌려보냈다.
ko.R: 헤롯과 그의 병사들은 예수를 아무것도 아닌 사람처럼 대하며 놀렸다. 그들은 마치 왕에게 입히듯이 예수께 번쩍이는 옷을 입혔다. 그러고 나서 헤롯은 예수를 빌라도에게 돌려보냈다.

decisions.choice: treated with contempt: treated as nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to count someone as nothing. It is used in Acts 4:11 of the stone the builders rejected (Psalm 118:22).

decisions.choice: bright clothing: a fine, shining robe put on him in mockery
alternatives: a white robe that showed he was innocent
decisions.reason: The word means bright or splendid. Dressing Jesus in a king's finery mocks his claim to be a king. Some think the robe also showed that Herod found him innocent, but Luke does not say so.

decisions.choice: troops: the soldiers of Herod's guard
decisions.reason: Herod had his own soldiers; the Roman soldiers mock Jesus later (23:36).

decisions.choice: as if he were a king
decisions.reason: Readable explains why the robe was mockery. The point is clear from the charge (23:2-3), but Luke does not spell it out.

decisions.choice: "một áo rực rỡ" (L); "một áo choàng lộng lẫy" (B); "một áo choàng sáng chói" (R)
decisions.reason: A fine, shining robe put on in mockery (meaning decision); "áo choàng" for a long outer robe, as in the Vietnamese Mark 15:17, while Literal keeps the Greek's plain "clothing".

decisions.choice: "병사들" for the troops; "조롱하다" (L, B), "놀리다" (R) for empaizo
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean Mark 15:16-20, so the two mockeries read alike.

decisions.choice: [그분께]
decisions.reason: Korean "입히다" needs the person dressed; the Greek leaves it understood, as the English Literal brackets it.

source.text: ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετ’ ἀλλήλων· προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς αὑτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Became then friends the both Herod and the Pilate on very the day with one another; were before for in enmity being toward themselves.

en.L: And both Herod and Pilate became friends with one another on that very day, for before [this] they had been at enmity with each other.
en.B: That same day Herod and Pilate became friends. Until then there had been hostility between them.
en.R: Herod and Pilate had been enemies before. But on that day they became friends.

es.L: Y Herodes y Pilato se hicieron amigos entre sí aquel mismo día, porque antes estaban enemistados el uno con el otro.
es.B: Aquel mismo día Herodes y Pilato se hicieron amigos. Hasta entonces había habido hostilidad entre ellos.
es.R: Herodes y Pilato habían sido enemigos. Pero ese día se hicieron amigos.

fr.L: Et Hérode et Pilate devinrent amis l’un de l’autre ce jour même ; car auparavant ils étaient en inimitié l’un avec l’autre.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, Hérode et Pilate devinrent amis ; jusque-là, il y avait de l’hostilité entre eux.
fr.R: Avant, Hérode et Pilate étaient ennemis. Mais ce jour-là, ils sont devenus amis.

sw.L: Na siku ile ile Herode na Pilato wakawa marafiki wao kwa wao, kwa maana hapo kabla walikuwa na uadui kati yao.
sw.B: Siku hiyo hiyo Herode na Pilato walifanyika marafiki. Kabla ya hapo kulikuwa na uhasama kati yao.
sw.R: Hapo kwanza Herode na Pilato walikuwa maadui. Lakini siku ile wakawa marafiki.

vi.L: Và ngay trong ngày ấy, Hê-rốt và Phi-lát trở thành bạn với nhau, vì trước [đó] họ vốn thù nghịch nhau.
vi.B: Ngay hôm ấy, Hê-rốt và Phi-lát trở thành bạn của nhau. Trước đó hai người vốn thù ghét nhau.
vi.R: Trước đây Hê-rốt và Phi-lát là kẻ thù của nhau. Nhưng ngay hôm ấy, họ trở thành bạn.

ko.L: 그리고 바로 그날 헤롯과 빌라도가 서로 친구가 되었다. 전에는 그들이 서로 원수로 지냈기 때문이다.
ko.B: 바로 그날 헤롯과 빌라도는 서로 친구가 되었다. 그전까지는 두 사람 사이에 적대감이 있었다.
ko.R: 헤롯과 빌라도는 전에 서로 원수였다. 그러나 그날 둘은 친구가 되었다.

decisions.choice: they had been at enmity: the cause is not told
decisions.reason: Luke does not say why they were enemies. Pilate's killing of some Galileans (13:1) may have offended Herod, who ruled Galilee, but that is a guess.

decisions.choice: Herod and Pilate became friends: rulers joined against the Lord's anointed
alternatives: a detail of no further meaning
decisions.reason: In Acts 4:25-27 the believers pray Psalm 2:1-2 and see it fulfilled when Herod and Pontius Pilate gathered against Jesus.

decisions.choice: the earlier enmity first
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened.

source.text: Πιλᾶτος δὲ συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τὸν λαὸν εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Προσηνέγκατέ μοι τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὡς ἀποστρέφοντα τὸν λαόν, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ἀνακρίνας οὐθὲν εὗρον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ αἴτιον ὧν κατηγορεῖτε κατ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Pilate then having called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people \v 14 said to them, You brought to me the man this as turning away the people, and behold I before you having examined nothing found in the man this guilt of which you accuse against him.

en.L: And Pilate called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people \v 14 and said to them, "You brought this man to me as one who turns the people away, and look, having examined [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] before you, I have found in this man no guilt of the things of which you accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers and the people \v 14 and said to them, "You brought this man before me on the charge that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was turning the people from their loyalty. I have questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in your presence, and I have found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} guilty of none of the things you accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} of.
en.R: Pilate called together the chief priests, the other leaders and the people. \v 14 He said to them, "You brought this man to me. You said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was getting the people to rebel. I have questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} here in front of you. But I have not found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} guilty of any of the things you say {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did.

es.L: Y Pilato, habiendo convocado a los jefes de los sacerdotes, a los dirigentes y al pueblo, \v 14 les dijo: «Me {{plural_you:trajeron|trajisteis}} a este hombre como a uno que extravía al pueblo; y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, yo, habiéndolo interrogado delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no he hallado en este hombre ninguna culpa de aquello de que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:acusan|acusáis}}.
es.B: Pilato reunió a los jefes de los sacerdotes, a los dirigentes y al pueblo, \v 14 y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes me trajeron|Vosotros me trajisteis}} a este hombre acusado de apartar al pueblo de su lealtad. Yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} he interrogado en presencia de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} he encontrado culpable de ninguna de las cosas de que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:acusan|acusáis}}.
es.R: Pilato reunió a los jefes de los sacerdotes, a los otros líderes y al pueblo. \v 14 Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes me trajeron|Vosotros me trajisteis}} a este hombre. {{plural_you:Dijeron|Dijisteis}} que estaba haciendo que el pueblo se rebelara. Yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} he interrogado aquí, delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Pero no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} he encontrado culpable de ninguna de las cosas que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} que hizo.

fr.L: Et Pilate, ayant convoqué les chefs des prêtres, les dirigeants et le peuple, \v 14 leur dit : « Vous m’avez amené cet homme comme détournant le peuple, et voici, moi, ayant enquêté devant vous, je n’ai trouvé en cet homme rien de coupable dans les choses dont vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accusez.
fr.B: Pilate réunit les chefs des prêtres, les dirigeants et le peuple, \v 14 et leur dit : « Vous m’avez amené cet homme en affirmant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} détournait le peuple de sa loyauté. Je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai interrogé devant vous, et je ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai trouvé coupable d’aucune des choses dont vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accusez.
fr.R: Pilate a réuni les chefs des prêtres, les autres dirigeants et le peuple. \v 14 Il leur a dit : « Vous m’avez amené cet homme. Vous avez dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} poussait le peuple à se révolter. Je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai interrogé ici, devant vous. Mais je n’ai trouvé aucune preuve qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ait fait ce que vous dites.

sw.L: Naye Pilato, akiisha kuwaita pamoja wakuu wa makuhani na viongozi na watu, \v 14 aliwaambia, "Mmeniletea mtu huyu kama mtu anayewapotosha watu; na tazama, mimi, nikiisha kumhoji mbele yenu, sikuona katika mtu huyu hatia yoyote ya mambo mnayomshtaki.
sw.B: Pilato aliwaita pamoja wakuu wa makuhani, viongozi na watu, \v 14 akawaambia, "Mlimleta mtu huyu kwangu kwa shtaka kwamba anawafanya watu waache utii wao. Nimemhoji mbele yenu, wala sikumwona na hatia ya lolote kati ya mambo mnayomshtaki.
sw.R: Pilato aliwaita pamoja wakuu wa makuhani, viongozi wengine na watu. \v 14 Akawaambia, "Mlimleta mtu huyu kwangu. Mlisema kwamba anawachochea watu waasi. Nimemhoji hapa mbele yenu. Lakini sikumwona na hatia ya jambo lolote kati ya yale mnayosema amefanya.

vi.L: Phi-lát triệu tập các thầy tế lễ cả, các nhà lãnh đạo và dân chúng, \v 14 rồi nói với họ: "Các người đã đem người này đến cho tôi như một kẻ xúi dân làm loạn, và kìa, chính tôi đã tra hỏi [ông ta] trước mặt các người mà không thấy người này có tội gì về những điều các người tố cáo ông ta.
vi.B: Phi-lát triệu tập các thầy tế lễ cả, các nhà lãnh đạo và dân chúng, \v 14 rồi nói với họ: "Các người đã giải người này đến cho tôi, cho rằng ông ta xúi dân chúng chống lại nhà cầm quyền. Tôi đã tra hỏi ông ta ngay trước mặt các người, nhưng không thấy ông ta có tội gì như các người tố cáo.
vi.R: Phi-lát gọi các thầy tế lễ cả, các nhà lãnh đạo khác và dân chúng đến. \v 14 Ông nói với họ: "Các người đã đem người này đến cho tôi. Các người nói ông ta xúi dân chúng nổi loạn. Tôi đã tra hỏi ông ta ngay trước mặt các người. Nhưng tôi không thấy ông ta có tội gì như các người nói.

ko.L: 그리고 빌라도는 대제사장들과 지도자들과 백성을 불러 모으고 \v 14 그들에게 말했다. "너희는 이 사람이 백성을 돌아서게 하는 자라고 하여 내게 끌고 왔다. 그리고 보라, 내가 너희 앞에서 [그를] 심문해 보았으나, 너희가 그를 고발하는 그 일들에 대하여 이 사람에게서 아무 죄도 찾지 못했다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 대제사장들과 지도자들과 백성을 불러 모으고 \v 14 그들에게 말했다. "너희는 이 사람이 백성을 선동하여 등을 돌리게 한다고 하면서 나에게 끌고 왔다. 내가 너희 앞에서 그를 심문해 보았지만, 너희가 고발하는 그 일들 가운데 어느 것에서도 이 사람의 죄를 찾지 못했다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 대제사장들과 다른 지도자들과 백성을 불러 모았다. \v 14 그리고 그들에게 말했다. "너희는 이 사람을 나에게 끌고 와서, 이 사람이 백성을 부추겨 반란을 일으키게 한다고 했다. 내가 너희 앞에서 이 사람을 직접 심문해 보았다. 그러나 너희가 고발한 일 가운데 이 사람이 잘못한 것은 하나도 찾지 못했다.

decisions.choice: turning the people away: inciting them to revolt
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn someone away, here from loyalty to their rulers. It sums up the charges of 23:2 and 23:5 with a different word.

decisions.choice: the second time Pilate declares Jesus innocent
decisions.reason: Pilate repeats the verdict of 23:4, now after a hearing in their presence (23:22 gives the third).

decisions.choice: the rulers: members of the council
decisions.reason: The same rulers appear at the cross (23:35) and in 24:20, where the two from Emmaus say that their rulers handed Jesus over.

decisions.choice: the people: now called in with their leaders
decisions.reason: Until now the people had been on Jesus' side, and the leaders feared them (20:19; 22:2). Here they are gathered with the leaders.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Pilate uses this word to point to his own verdict. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: getting the people to rebel
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of turning away was charged, as 23:2 and 23:5 show.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the verbs and pronouns addressed to the leaders and the people (trajeron|trajisteis, ustedes|vosotros, acusan|acusáis); "miren|mirad" for the Literal "look"
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" (the default) and Peninsular "vosotros"; the reader setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the chapter, also in Jesus's words to the women (23:28-30).

decisions.choice: los dirigentes (L, B); los otros líderes (R)
decisions.reason: The rulers here are members of the Jewish council (meaning decision m3), not heads of state, which "gobernantes" would suggest. The same in 23:35.

decisions.choice: voici (L); not rendered as a separate word (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "voici" is still natural for pointing to something, so Literal keeps it where the English Literal says "look"; Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as the English does. The same in 23:15, 23:29 and 23:50.

decisions.choice: "các nhà lãnh đạo" for "the rulers"
decisions.reason: Members of the ruling council (meaning decision); "các nhà lãnh đạo" names them plainly and is used again in 23:35 and 24:20.

decisions.choice: "ông ta" in Pilate's mouth, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Pilate's own word for Jesus, as in the Vietnamese Mark 15:12 and Matthew 27:23; it has no reverent capital form, so the English spans in his speech have no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "보라" (L) for idou; not rendered (B, R), here and through chapters 23-24
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek attention word with the short written form "보라"; in Balanced and Readable it has no separate word, as in English.

decisions.choice: Pilate speaks of Jesus as "이 사람" and "그" with no honorific
decisions.reason: A Roman official speaking of a prisoner, as in the Korean Mark 15:14; the narrator still honours Jesus.

source.text: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ Ἡρῴδης, ἀνέπεμψεν γὰρ αὐτὸν πρὸς ἡμᾶς· καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐδὲν ἄξιον θανάτου ἐστὶν πεπραγμένον αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: But not even Herod, he sent back for him to us; and behold nothing worthy of death is having been done by him;

en.L: Neither [did] Herod, for he sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to us; and look, nothing deserving death has been done by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Neither did Herod, for he sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to us. Plainly {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done nothing that deserves death.
en.R: Herod did not find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} guilty either. That is why he sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to us. This man has done nothing that deserves the death penalty.

es.L: Pero tampoco Herodes, pues nos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} devolvió; y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, nada digno de muerte ha sido hecho por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Ni Herodes tampoco, pues nos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} devolvió. Está claro que no ha hecho nada que merezca la muerte.
es.R: Herodes tampoco {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontró culpable. Por eso nos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} devolvió. Este hombre no ha hecho nada que merezca la pena de muerte.

fr.L: Mais Hérode non plus, car il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a renvoyé vers nous ; et voici, rien qui mérite la mort n’a été fait par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Hérode non plus, puisqu’il nous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a renvoyé. Il est clair qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a rien fait qui mérite la mort.
fr.R: Hérode non plus ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a pas trouvé coupable. C’est pour cela qu’il nous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a renvoyé. Cet homme n’a rien fait qui mérite la peine de mort.

sw.L: Wala Herode, kwa maana alimrudisha kwetu; na tazama, hakuna lolote linalostahili kifo lililotendwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Wala Herode hakumwona na hatia, kwa maana amemrudisha kwetu. Ni wazi kwamba hajafanya jambo lolote linalostahili kifo.
sw.R: Herode naye hakumwona na hatia. Ndiyo sababu alimrudisha kwetu. Mtu huyu hajafanya lolote linalostahili adhabu ya kifo.

vi.L: Ngay cả Hê-rốt cũng không [thấy], vì ông ấy đã giải ông ta trả lại cho chúng ta; và kìa, ông ta chẳng làm điều gì đáng chết cả.
vi.B: Hê-rốt cũng không thấy, vì ông ấy đã gửi ông ta trả về đây. Rõ ràng ông ta không làm điều gì đáng tội chết.
vi.R: Hê-rốt cũng không thấy ông ta có tội. Vì vậy Hê-rốt mới gửi ông ta trả về đây. Người này không làm điều gì đáng bị xử tử cả.

ko.L: 헤롯도 [찾지 못했다]. 그가 그를 우리에게 돌려보냈기 때문이다. 그리고 보라, 그가 한 일 가운데 죽어야 할 만한 것은 아무것도 없다.
ko.B: 헤롯도 마찬가지였다. 그래서 그를 우리에게 돌려보낸 것이다. 분명히 이 사람은 죽어야 할 만한 일을 하나도 하지 않았다.
ko.R: 헤롯도 이 사람에게서 아무 죄도 찾지 못했다. 그래서 이 사람을 우리에게 돌려보냈다. 이 사람은 사형을 받을 만한 일을 하나도 하지 않았다.

decisions.choice: he sent him back to us: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: I sent you to him, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: The early papyrus P75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus read "he sent him back to us". Many other manuscripts, Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Bezae among them, read "I sent you to him". The meaning is much the same: Herod too found nothing. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: nothing worthy of death: no crime that carries the death penalty
decisions.reason: The phrase is a legal one. Paul's case is described in the same words in Acts 23:29 and 26:31.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into 23:16
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the verse with a raised dot; Pilate's conclusion follows in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Pilate uses this word to stress his conclusion. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: Herod did not find him guilty either
decisions.reason: Readable supplies what Herod did not do, which the Greek leaves to be understood from 23:14.

decisions.choice: inclusive "chúng ta" (L); "về đây" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose whether "us" includes the hearers; the case now lies before all who are gathered, so Literal says "chúng ta", and Balanced and Readable avoid the choice with "về đây".

decisions.choice: [찾지 못했다]
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "nor Herod"; Korean needs the verb, taken from 23:14.

source.text: παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω.

records.literal_gloss: Having punished therefore him I will release [him].

en.L: Therefore I will punish {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and release [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]."
en.B: So I will have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} flogged and then let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} go."
en.R: So I will have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} whipped, and then I will let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} go free."

es.L: Así que, después de castigarlo, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} soltaré».
es.B: Así que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} haré azotar y luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} soltaré».
es.R: Así que voy a mandar que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azoten, y después {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejaré libre».

fr.L: Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} châtierai donc et [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] relâcherai. »
fr.B: Je vais donc {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire flageller, puis je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} relâcherai. »
fr.R: Alors je vais {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire frapper à coups de fouet, et puis je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laisserai partir. »

sw.L: Basi, nikiisha kumwadhibu, nitamfungua."
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nitaamuru apigwe mijeledi, kisha nitamwachilia."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nitaagiza achapwe viboko, kisha nitamwachilia huru."

vi.L: Vậy tôi sẽ trừng phạt ông ta rồi tha [ông ta]."
vi.B: Vì vậy, tôi sẽ cho đánh đòn ông ta rồi thả ra."
vi.R: Vì vậy, tôi sẽ cho lính lấy roi đánh ông ta, rồi thả ông ta ra."

ko.L: 그러므로 나는 그를 징계하고 놓아주겠다."
ko.B: 그러니 그를 매질하게 한 뒤에 풀어 주겠다."
ko.R: 그러니 이 사람을 매로 때리게 한 다음에 풀어 주겠다."

decisions.choice: punish: a beating as a warning, short of death
alternatives: the scourging that came before crucifixion
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to train or discipline. Here it is a lighter beating meant to teach a lesson, offered so that Jesus could then be released.

decisions.choice: no verse 17: the SBLGNT has no verse here
alternatives: verse 17, "Now he was obliged to release one man to them at the feast", found in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add a sentence saying that Pilate had to release one prisoner at the feast; Codex Bezae has it after 23:19 instead. It is missing from the early papyrus P75 and from Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus, and its changing position suggests it was added from Mark 15:6 or Matthew 27:15. The verse number is therefore skipped, and the text goes on at 23:18. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: have him flogged (B); have him whipped (R)
decisions.reason: A governor would order soldiers to do the beating; Balanced and Readable say what kind of punishment was meant.

decisions.choice: "trừng phạt" (L); "cho đánh đòn" (B); "cho lính lấy roi đánh" (R)
decisions.reason: A beating as a warning, short of death (meaning decision); "đánh roi" is kept for the flogging before crucifixion in Mark 15:15, so the two are not confused.

decisions.choice: "징계하다" (L), "매질하게 하다" (B), "매로 때리게 하다" (R) for paideuo; "놓아주다" (L), "풀어 주다" (B, R) for apolyo, here and in 23:22
decisions.reason: A beating as a warning (meaning decision), a different word from the flogging of Mark 15:15 ("채찍질하다"); the release verbs are those of the Korean Mark 15:6-15.

source.text: Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες· Αἶρε τοῦτον, ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν τὸν Βαραββᾶν·

records.literal_gloss: They cried out however all together saying, Take away this [man], release now to us the Barabbas;

en.L: But they all cried out together, saying, "Away with this man, and release Barabbas to us!"
en.B: But the whole crowd shouted as one, "Take this man away! Set Barabbas free for us!"
en.R: But the whole crowd shouted together, "Kill this man! Let Barabbas go free for us!"

es.L: Pero gritaron todos juntos, diciendo: «¡Quita de en medio a este, y suéltanos a Barrabás!».
es.B: Pero toda la multitud gritó a una voz: «¡Llévate a este! ¡Suéltanos a Barrabás!».
es.R: Pero toda la gente gritó a la vez: «¡Mata a este hombre! ¡Deja libre a Barrabás!».

fr.L: Mais ils s’écrièrent tous ensemble, disant : « Enlève celui-ci, et relâche-nous Barabbas ! »
fr.B: Mais toute la foule cria d’une seule voix : « Emmène cet homme ! Libère-nous Barabbas ! »
fr.R: Mais toute la foule a crié en même temps : « Fais mourir cet homme ! Libère-nous Barabbas ! »

sw.L: Lakini wakapiga kelele wote pamoja, wakisema, "Mwondoe huyu, utufungulie Baraba!"
sw.B: Lakini umati wote ulipiga kelele kwa pamoja, "Mwondoe mtu huyu! Utufungulie Baraba!"
sw.R: Lakini umati wote ulipiga kelele pamoja, "Muue mtu huyu! Mwachilie Baraba kwa ajili yetu!"

vi.L: Nhưng tất cả cùng nhau la lên: "Trừ khử người này đi, và tha Ba-ra-ba cho chúng tôi!"
vi.B: Nhưng cả đám đông đồng thanh la lên: "Trừ khử người này đi! Thả Ba-ra-ba cho chúng tôi!"
vi.R: Nhưng cả đám đông cùng la lên: "Giết người này đi! Thả Ba-ra-ba cho chúng tôi!"

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 다 함께 소리 질러 말했다. "이 자를 없애 버리시오! 그리고 바라바를 우리에게 놓아주시오!"
ko.B: 그러자 무리가 한목소리로 소리쳤다. "이 사람을 없애 버리시오! 바라바를 풀어 주시오!"
ko.R: 그러나 무리가 다 함께 소리쳤다. "이 사람을 죽이시오! 바라바를 풀어 주시오!"

decisions.choice: Away with this man: a demand that he be put to death
alternatives: send him out of the city
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up and take away. The crowd in Jerusalem shouts the same words at Paul, adding "from the earth" (Acts 21:36; 22:22).

decisions.choice: Barabbas: a prisoner the crowd wanted freed
decisions.reason: The name is Aramaic for "son of the father". Luke introduces him only here and explains who he was in the next sentence. Because the SBLGNT has no verse 17, Luke does not mention the custom of releasing a prisoner at the feast that the other Gospels describe (Mark 15:6).

decisions.choice: a raised dot: the description of Barabbas follows
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT closes this sentence with a raised dot; the next one is a relative clause about Barabbas.

decisions.choice: Kill
decisions.reason: Readable says what the demand meant, as Acts 22:22 makes clear.

decisions.choice: "Trừ khử" (L, B); "Giết" (R)
decisions.reason: The cry demands his death (meaning decision); a literal "take away" would not say that in Vietnamese, while "trừ khử" (get rid of) keeps the Greek's indirectness at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: "없애 버리시오" (L, B); "죽이시오" (R)
decisions.reason: The cry demands his death (meaning decision); "없애 버리다" says that without losing the picture of taking away, and Readable says it outright, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ.

records.literal_gloss: who was because of an uprising certain having happened in the city and murder having been thrown in the prison.

en.L: He was [a man] who had been thrown into prison for a certain uprising that had taken place in the city, and for murder.
en.B: He had been put in prison for a riot that broke out in the city, and for murder.
en.R: Barabbas was in prison because he had taken part in a revolt in the city. He had also murdered someone.

es.L: Este era [uno] que había sido echado en la cárcel por cierta revuelta ocurrida en la ciudad, y por homicidio.
es.B: Lo habían metido en la cárcel por un motín que hubo en la ciudad, y por asesinato.
es.R: Barrabás estaba en la cárcel porque había participado en una rebelión en la ciudad. Además, había matado a alguien.

fr.L: [C’était un homme] qui avait été jeté en prison à cause d’une certaine émeute survenue dans la ville, et pour un meurtre.
fr.B: Il avait été mis en prison pour une émeute qui avait éclaté dans la ville, et pour meurtre.
fr.R: Barabbas était en prison parce qu’il avait pris part à une révolte dans la ville. Il avait aussi tué quelqu’un.

sw.L: Huyo alikuwa [mtu] aliyetupwa gerezani kwa sababu ya uasi fulani uliotokea mjini, na kwa mauaji.
sw.B: Alikuwa ametiwa gerezani kwa sababu ya ghasia zilizotokea mjini, na kwa kosa la mauaji.
sw.R: Baraba alikuwa gerezani kwa sababu alishiriki katika uasi uliotokea mjini. Tena alikuwa ameua mtu.

vi.L: Kẻ này đã bị tống vào ngục vì một cuộc nổi loạn đã xảy ra trong thành, và vì tội giết người.
vi.B: Hắn đã bị bỏ tù vì một cuộc bạo loạn xảy ra trong thành và vì tội giết người.
vi.R: Ba-ra-ba đang ở tù vì đã tham gia một cuộc nổi loạn trong thành. Hắn cũng đã giết người.

ko.L: 그는 성안에서 일어난 어떤 반란과 살인 때문에 감옥에 던져진 [사람]이었다.
ko.B: 바라바는 성안에서 일어난 폭동과 살인 때문에 감옥에 갇혀 있던 사람이었다.
ko.R: 바라바는 성안에서 폭동에 가담했다가 감옥에 갇혀 있었다. 그는 사람을 죽이기도 했다.

decisions.choice: uprising: a revolt against the authorities
decisions.reason: The word is used for civil unrest and rebellion (Acts 19:40). The man released was guilty of the very thing Jesus was falsely charged with (23:2, 5, 14).

decisions.choice: who: a relative clause continuing the last sentence
decisions.reason: The Greek describes Barabbas in a clause that hangs on his name in 23:18.

decisions.choice: He was (L); He had (B); Barabbas (R)
decisions.reason: Every level starts a new sentence and supplies a subject.

decisions.choice: "Kẻ này" (L), "Hắn" (B, R) for Barabbas
decisions.reason: The narrator's plain words for a man jailed for revolt and murder; "hắn" is the narrator's word for wrongdoers elsewhere in the Vietnamese Luke.

decisions.choice: "반란" (L), "폭동" (B, R) for stasis
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean Mark 15:7 for the same uprising.

source.text: πάλιν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος προσεφώνησεν, θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: Again then the Pilate called to [them], wishing to release the Jesus.

en.L: And Pilate called out to [them] again, wishing to release Jesus.
en.B: Pilate spoke to them once more, because he wanted to set Jesus free.
en.R: Pilate wanted to let Jesus go. So he spoke to the crowd again.

es.L: Y de nuevo Pilato [les] habló, queriendo soltar a Jesús.
es.B: Pilato les habló una vez más, porque quería poner en libertad a Jesús.
es.R: Pilato quería dejar libre a Jesús. Por eso volvió a hablarle a la gente.

fr.L: Et de nouveau Pilate [leur] adressa la parole, voulant relâcher Jésus.
fr.B: Pilate leur parla encore une fois, car il voulait libérer Jésus.
fr.R: Pilate voulait laisser partir Jésus. Alors il a encore parlé à la foule.

sw.L: Naye Pilato akasema [nao] tena, akitaka kumfungua Yesu.
sw.B: Pilato aliongea nao tena, kwa sababu alitaka kumwachilia Yesu.
sw.R: Pilato alitaka kumwachilia Yesu. Kwa hiyo akasema na umati tena.

vi.L: Phi-lát lại nói với [họ], vì muốn tha Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Phi-lát lên tiếng với họ một lần nữa, vì ông muốn thả Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Phi-lát muốn thả Đức Giê-xu. Vì vậy ông lại nói với đám đông.

ko.L: 그러자 빌라도가 예수를 놓아주기를 원하여 다시 [그들에게] 소리쳐 말했다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 예수를 풀어 주고 싶어서, 다시 그들에게 말했다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 예수를 풀어 주고 싶었다. 그래서 다시 무리에게 말했다.

decisions.choice: wishing to release Jesus: Pilate's will against theirs
decisions.reason: Luke shows Pilate wanting to release Jesus three times (23:16, 20, 22). In the end he hands Jesus over to their will (23:25).

decisions.choice: his wish first, then his speaking
decisions.reason: Readable states the reason first, which is easier to follow.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες· Σταύρου σταύρου αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: They but were shouting saying, Crucify, crucify him.

en.L: But they kept shouting, saying, "Crucify, crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.B: But they kept shouting back, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: But they kept on shouting, "Nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross! Nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross!"

es.L: Pero ellos gritaban, diciendo: «¡Crucifícalo, crucifícalo!».
es.B: Pero ellos seguían gritando: «¡Crucifícalo! ¡Crucifícalo!».
es.R: Pero ellos seguían gritando: «¡Clávalo en una cruz! ¡Clávalo en una cruz!».

fr.L: Mais eux criaient, disant : « Crucifie, crucifie-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! »
fr.B: Mais ils criaient en retour : « Crucifie-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! Crucifie-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! »
fr.R: Mais ils continuaient à crier : « Fais-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} clouer sur une croix ! Fais-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} clouer sur une croix ! »

sw.L: Lakini wao walikuwa wakipiga kelele, wakisema, "Msulubishe, msulubishe!"
sw.B: Lakini wao waliendelea kupiga kelele, "Msulubishe! Msulubishe!"
sw.R: Lakini waliendelea kupiga kelele, "Mpigilie misumari msalabani! Mpigilie misumari msalabani!"

vi.L: Nhưng họ cứ la lên: "Đóng đinh, đóng đinh ông ta!"
vi.B: Nhưng họ cứ la lại: "Đóng đinh ông ta đi! Đóng đinh ông ta đi!"
vi.R: Nhưng họ cứ la lên: "Hãy đóng đinh ông ta trên cây thập tự! Hãy đóng đinh ông ta trên cây thập tự!"

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 계속 소리 질러 말했다. "십자가에 못 박으시오, 그를 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 계속 맞받아 외쳤다. "십자가에 못 박으시오! 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.R: 그러나 사람들은 계속 소리쳤다. "저 사람을 십자가에 못 박으시오! 십자가에 못 박으시오!"

decisions.choice: kept shouting ... Crucify, crucify: a continuing, repeated cry
decisions.reason: The verb is imperfect, and the command is present tense and doubled: they shouted it over and over.

decisions.choice: crucify: the Roman death penalty on a cross
decisions.reason: Rome crucified slaves, rebels and violent criminals. The condemned man was nailed or tied to a wooden cross and left to die in public, a death meant to shame.

decisions.choice: Nail him to a cross
decisions.reason: Readable explains what crucifixion was, as in 24:7.

decisions.choice: crucifier (L, B); Fais-le clouer sur une croix (R), and "clouer sur une croix" in the narration of 23:33
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:13: Readable explains crucifixion as the English does, and the crowd speaks to Pilate, who would order the execution rather than carry it out, so French says "fais-le clouer".

decisions.choice: "ông ta" for Jesus in the crowd's cry, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:13: the crowd would not use the reverent "ngài", and their word has no capital form.

decisions.choice: "đóng đinh ... trên cây thập tự" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "on the cross" so a new reader sees what kind of death is meant, as in the Vietnamese Mark 15:13.

decisions.choice: "십자가에 못 박다" for stauroo at every level, through chapters 23-24
decisions.reason: The word of the Korean Mark 15:13 and John 19:6; it already says "nail to a cross", so Readable needs no other wording.

source.text: ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος;

records.literal_gloss: The but a third [time] said to them, What for evil did this [man]?

en.L: And a third time he said to them, "Why, what evil has this man done?
en.B: For the third time he said to them, "Why? What wrong has this man done?
en.R: Pilate spoke to them a third time. He said, "Why? What has this man done wrong?

es.L: Y él por tercera vez les dijo: «Pues ¿qué mal ha hecho este?
es.B: Por tercera vez les dijo: «¿Por qué? ¿Qué mal ha hecho este hombre?
es.R: Pilato les habló por tercera vez. Les dijo: «¿Por qué? ¿Qué ha hecho de malo este hombre?

fr.L: Et pour la troisième fois il leur dit : « Quel mal a donc fait celui-ci ?
fr.B: Pour la troisième fois, il leur dit : « Pourquoi ? Quel mal cet homme a-t-il fait ?
fr.R: Pilate leur a parlé une troisième fois. Il a dit : « Pourquoi ? Qu’est-ce que cet homme a fait de mal ?

sw.L: Naye akawaambia mara ya tatu, "Kwani, huyu amefanya ubaya gani?
sw.B: Kwa mara ya tatu aliwaambia, "Kwa nini? Mtu huyu amefanya kosa gani?
sw.R: Pilato aliongea nao mara ya tatu. Akasema, "Kwa nini? Mtu huyu amefanya baya gani?

vi.L: Ông nói với họ lần thứ ba: "Sao vậy, người này đã làm điều ác gì?
vi.B: Phi-lát nói với họ lần thứ ba: "Tại sao? Người này đã làm điều gì sai trái?
