vi.R: Chúng ta đáng bị phạt. Chúng ta đang nhận lấy điều chúng ta đáng phải chịu vì những việc chúng ta đã làm. Nhưng người này chưa hề làm điều gì sai."

ko.L: 그리고 우리는 마땅히 [이런 벌을 받는다]. 우리가 한 일에 합당한 것을 받고 있기 때문이다. 그러나 이 사람은 아무 잘못된 일도 하지 않았다."
ko.B: 우리는 당연히 벌을 받는 것이다. 우리가 저지른 일의 대가를 받고 있으니까. 그러나 이분은 아무 잘못도 하지 않으셨다."
ko.R: 우리는 벌을 받아도 싸다. 우리가 한 나쁜 짓에 대한 대가를 받는 것이다. 그러나 이분은 아무 잘못도 하지 않으셨다."

decisions.choice: out of place: improper, wrong in any way
alternatives: only no crime worthy of death
decisions.reason: The word means out of place or unfitting. The criminal says more than that Jesus is innocent of the charge: he has done nothing wrong at all.

decisions.choice: this man did nothing wrong: another witness to his innocence
decisions.reason: Pilate (23:4, 14, 22), Herod (23:15), this criminal and the centurion (23:47) all speak of Jesus as innocent.

decisions.choice: justly: rightly, as the law requires
decisions.reason: The adverb is formed from the word the centurion uses of Jesus in 23:47: the criminals suffer justly, but Jesus is just.

decisions.choice: [are suffering]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood; Literal supplies it in brackets.

decisions.choice: inclusive "chúng ta"
decisions.reason: The speaker includes the man he is rebuking: both are under the same sentence.

decisions.choice: [이런 벌을 받는다]
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "justly"; the verb is understood, as the English Literal brackets it.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Ἰησοῦ, μνήσθητί μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying, Jesus, remember me when you come in the kingdom of you.

en.L: And he was saying, "Jesus, remember me when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom."
en.B: Then he said, "Jesus, remember me when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom."
en.R: Then he said, "Jesus, please remember me when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come as king."

es.L: Y decía: «Jesús, acuérdate de mí cuando vengas en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino».
es.B: Después dijo: «Jesús, cuando vengas en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino, acuérdate de mí».
es.R: Luego dijo: «Jesús, por favor, acuérdate de mí cuando vengas como rey».

fr.L: Et il disait : « Jésus, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de moi quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viendras dans {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} royaume. »
fr.B: Puis il dit : « Jésus, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de moi lorsque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viendras dans {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} royaume. »
fr.R: Puis il a dit : « Jésus, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de moi quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viendras comme roi. »

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akisema, "Yesu, nikumbuke wakati utakapokuja ndani ya ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."
sw.B: Kisha akasema, "Yesu, utakapokuja katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, unikumbuke."
sw.R: Kisha akasema, "Yesu, tafadhali unikumbuke utakapokuja kama mfalme."

vi.L: Rồi người ấy nói: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, xin nhớ đến tôi khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến trong vương quốc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.B: Rồi anh ta nói: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, xin nhớ đến tôi khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến trong vương quốc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.R: Rồi anh ta nói: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến làm vua, xin nhớ đến tôi."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "예수님, 예수님의 나라에 오실 때에 저를 기억해 주십시오."
ko.B: 그리고 그가 말했다. "예수님, 예수님의 나라에 오실 때에 저를 기억해 주십시오."
ko.R: 그리고 그가 말했다. "예수님, 왕으로 오실 때에 저를 꼭 기억해 주십시오."

decisions.choice: in your kingdom: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: into your kingdom, the reading of the early papyrus P75 and Codex Vaticanus
decisions.reason: Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Alexandrinus, Codex Ephraemi and most later manuscripts read "in your kingdom", that is, when Jesus comes in royal power (9:26). P75 and Codex Vaticanus read "into your kingdom", when he enters his reign (compare 24:26). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: remember me: think of me with favor and act for me
decisions.reason: In Scripture to ask someone to remember you is to ask for their help (Genesis 40:14; 1 Samuel 1:11; Psalm 106:4).

decisions.choice: when you come in your kingdom: the criminal believes that Jesus is a king
decisions.reason: Where the others mock the title on the notice, this man trusts that Jesus will reign after his death.

decisions.choice: when you come as king
alternatives: when you come in your kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable says what coming in his kingdom means.

decisions.choice: souviens-toi, with "toi" under the deity_pronoun setting
alternatives: no span on the reflexive pronoun
decisions.reason: French "se souvenir" carries a pronoun for the person addressed, here Jesus, so it takes the setting, though the English "remember" has no pronoun; so does "s’il te plaît" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu", "tôi" for himself, and "ngài" (with the deity_pronoun span) for "you"
decisions.reason: As the blind man pleads in the Vietnamese Mark 10:47: "Lạy" is a humble plea and the bare name would be disrespectful. Addressed in the second person, "ngài" carries the setting, as in the Vietnamese Luke 8:28.

decisions.choice: "예수님" and 합쇼체 with "저"; "예수님의 나라" for "your kingdom" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Korean addresses someone honoured by title rather than by "당신", which would sound distant or rude here; repeating the title is the natural Korean way to say "your".

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀμήν σοι λέγω σήμερον μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, Truly to you I say today with me you will be in the paradise.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in paradise."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "Truly I tell you, this very day you will be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in paradise."
en.R: Jesus answered him, "I tell you the truth: before this day is over, you will be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in paradise."

es.L: Y le dijo: «En verdad te digo: hoy estarás conmigo en el paraíso».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «En verdad te digo que hoy mismo estarás conmigo en el paraíso».
es.R: Jesús le contestó: «Te digo la verdad: antes de que termine este día, estarás conmigo en el paraíso».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « En vérité, je te le dis, aujourd’hui tu seras avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} dans le paradis. »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « En vérité, je te le dis, aujourd’hui même tu seras avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} dans le paradis. »
fr.R: Jésus lui a répondu : « Je te le dis, c’est la vérité : avant la fin de ce jour, tu seras avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} dans le paradis. »

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Kweli nakuambia, leo utakuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} katika paradiso."
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Kweli nakuambia, leo hii utakuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} katika paradiso."
sw.R: Yesu alimjibu, "Nakuambia ukweli: kabla siku hii haijaisha, utakuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} katika paradiso."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với anh ta: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với anh, hôm nay anh sẽ ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong Ba-ra-đi."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với anh, ngay hôm nay anh sẽ ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong Ba-ra-đi."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời anh ta: "Ta nói thật với anh: ngay trong ngày hôm nay, anh sẽ ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên thiên đàng."

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그에게 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너에게 말한다. 오늘 네가 나와 함께 낙원에 있을 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너에게 말한다. 바로 오늘 네가 나와 함께 낙원에 있을 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "내가 너에게 분명히 말한다. 오늘이 다 가기 전에 너는 나와 함께 낙원에 있을 것이다."

decisions.choice: today goes with what follows: today you will be with me
alternatives: I tell you today: you will be with me
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has no comma here. Jesus' sayings that begin "Truly I tell you" do not add "today" to the opening words, and Luke often uses "today" for salvation that comes now (2:11; 4:21; 19:9).

decisions.choice: paradise: the place of the righteous dead with God
decisions.reason: The word, from Persian, means a garden or park. The Greek version of the Old Testament used it for the garden of Eden (Genesis 2:8), and it came to mean the place where God's people are with him (2 Corinthians 12:4; Revelation 2:7).

decisions.choice: today ... with me: more than the man asked
decisions.reason: He asked to be remembered when Jesus comes as king. Jesus promises that he will be with him that same day.

decisions.choice: before this day is over
decisions.reason: Readable stresses how soon the promise will come true.

decisions.choice: En verdad te digo (L, B); Te digo la verdad (R)
alternatives: Les digo (the plural of the term sheet)
decisions.reason: The set rendering of Jesus's single "amen" across these drafts, here in the singular because he speaks to one man. "Conmigo" is joined to the preposition and takes no deity_pronoun span, as the term sheet sets.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je te le dis (L, B); Je te le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
decisions.reason: The formula of the book (4:24) with the singular "te", since Jesus speaks to one man; "aujourd’hui" follows it, as the meaning decision reads the sentence (m1).

decisions.choice: Kweli nakuambia (L, B); Nakuambia ukweli (R)
alternatives: Kweli nawaambia (the plural of the term sheet)
decisions.reason: The set rendering of Jesus's single "amen" across these drafts, here in the singular because he speaks to one man.

decisions.choice: paradiso (every level)
decisions.reason: The place of the righteous dead with God (meaning decision m2). "Paradiso" keeps the Greek word, as the Spanish and English do; "peponi" is the familiar Swahili word for paradise and a reviewer may prefer it, especially at Readable.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với anh" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với anh" (R); Jesus calls the man "anh"
decisions.reason: The settled form for the amen saying, as in the Vietnamese Luke 4:24; "anh" is how Jesus speaks to a grown man in the Vietnamese Luke 8:39.

decisions.choice: "Ba-ra-đi" (L, B); "thiên đàng" (R)
decisions.reason: The borrowed word for paradise, the place of the righteous dead with God (meaning decision); Readable uses the everyday word for where God's people go.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 너에게 분명히 말한다" (R); "오늘" after the formula
decisions.reason: The settled Korean amen formula, with the singular "너에게" of Mark 14:30. The formula closes with its own full stop, so "오늘" plainly belongs to what follows (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "낙원" at every level
decisions.reason: The established Korean word for paradise, the place of the righteous dead with God (meaning decision); "천국" is kept for the kingdom of heaven.

source.text: Καὶ ἦν ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος, ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον.

records.literal_gloss: And it was already about [the] hour sixth, and darkness came over all the land until [the] hour ninth, \v 45 the sun having failed, was torn then the curtain of the sanctuary in [the] middle.

en.L: And it was already about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour, \v 45 the sun['s light] having failed; and the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in the middle.
en.B: It was already about midday when darkness covered the whole land, and it lasted until three in the afternoon. \v 45 The light of the sun failed, and the curtain in the sanctuary was torn down the middle.
en.R: It was now about the middle of the day. Then the whole land became dark, and it stayed dark until three in the afternoon. \v 45 The sun's light failed. And the heavy curtain in the temple was torn right down the middle.

es.L: Y era ya como la hora sexta, y vino oscuridad sobre toda la tierra hasta la hora novena, \v 45 habiendo faltado [la luz del] sol; y la cortina del santuario fue rasgada por en medio.
es.B: Era ya como el mediodía cuando la oscuridad cubrió toda la tierra, y duró hasta las tres de la tarde. \v 45 La luz del sol faltó, y la cortina del santuario fue rasgada por la mitad.
es.R: Era ya como el mediodía. Entonces toda la tierra se quedó a oscuras, y siguió oscuro hasta las tres de la tarde. \v 45 La luz del sol se apagó. Y la gruesa cortina del templo fue rasgada justo por la mitad.

fr.L: Et c’était déjà environ la sixième heure, et l’obscurité se fit sur tout le pays jusqu’à la neuvième heure, \v 45 le soleil ayant fait défaut ; et le voile du sanctuaire fut déchiré par le milieu.
fr.B: Il était déjà environ midi quand l’obscurité se fit sur tout le pays ; elle dura jusqu’à quinze heures. \v 45 Le soleil cessa de briller, et le voile du sanctuaire se déchira par le milieu.
fr.R: C’était déjà le milieu de la journée. Puis tout le pays est devenu sombre, et il a fait noir jusqu’à trois heures de l’après-midi. \v 45 Le soleil ne donnait plus de lumière. Et le grand rideau du temple a été déchiré en deux, par le milieu.

sw.L: Na ilikuwa tayari yapata saa sita, na giza likaja juu ya nchi yote mpaka saa tisa, \v 45 jua likiwa limeshindwa [kutoa nuru]; na pazia la patakatifu likapasuliwa katikati.
sw.B: Ilikuwa tayari yapata saa sita mchana giza lilipoifunika nchi yote, likadumu mpaka saa tisa alasiri. \v 45 Nuru ya jua ilitoweka, na pazia la patakatifu likapasuliwa katikati.
sw.R: Ilikuwa sasa yapata saa sita mchana. Kisha nchi yote ikawa giza, na giza hilo likaendelea mpaka saa tisa alasiri. \v 45 Jua liliacha kutoa nuru. Na lile pazia zito la hekalu likapasuliwa katikati kabisa.

vi.L: Lúc ấy đã khoảng giờ thứ sáu, và bóng tối bao trùm khắp cả xứ cho đến giờ thứ chín, \v 45 mặt trời thôi [chiếu sáng]; và bức màn của đền thờ bị xé ra ở giữa.
vi.B: Lúc ấy đã khoảng giữa trưa. Bóng tối bao phủ khắp xứ cho đến ba giờ chiều. \v 45 Mặt trời không còn chiếu sáng, và bức màn trong đền thờ bị xé đôi ở giữa.
vi.R: Lúc ấy là khoảng mười hai giờ trưa. Rồi cả xứ trở nên tối tăm, và trời tối như vậy cho đến ba giờ chiều. \v 45 Mặt trời không còn chiếu sáng. Bức màn dày trong đền thờ bị xé toạc làm hai.

ko.L: 그리고 이미 여섯째 시쯤 되었는데, 온 땅에 어둠이 임하여 아홉째 시까지 계속되었다. \v 45 해가 [빛을] 잃었고, 성소의 휘장이 한가운데가 찢어졌다.
ko.B: 그때가 벌써 낮 열두 시쯤이었는데, 온 땅에 어둠이 덮여 오후 세 시까지 계속되었다. \v 45 해가 빛을 잃었다. 그리고 성소의 휘장이 한가운데가 둘로 찢어졌다.
ko.R: 어느새 낮 열두 시쯤이 되었다. 그때 온 땅이 캄캄해지더니 오후 세 시까지 계속 어두웠다. \v 45 햇빛이 사라졌다. 그리고 성전 안에 드리워져 있던 휘장이 한가운데가 찢어졌다.

decisions.choice: the sixth hour to the ninth: from about noon to about three in the afternoon
alternatives: six and nine in the morning
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise, at about six in the morning.

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Israel
decisions.reason: The word can mean land or earth. Luke may mean only the land around Jerusalem, or the whole world.

decisions.choice: the sun having failed: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sun was darkened, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: The early papyrus P75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus read "the sun having failed". Many later manuscripts read "and the sun was darkened". The verb of the earlier reading can be used of an eclipse, but a solar eclipse cannot happen at Passover, which fell at full moon, nor last three hours; it may be the plain sense, that the sun's light failed, which every level gives. Some think copyists changed the word to avoid the idea of an eclipse. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the curtain of the sanctuary: a curtain in the temple building itself
alternatives: a curtain in the outer courts
decisions.reason: The sanctuary was the building that held the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place. A curtain separated the two (Exodus 26:31-33), and another hung at its entrance; Luke does not say which. Hebrews 10:19-20 speaks of the way into God's presence opened through Jesus' flesh, as through the curtain.

decisions.choice: darkness at midday: a sign of God's judgment
decisions.reason: Amos 8:9 speaks of a day when God would make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

decisions.choice: midday ... three in the afternoon
alternatives: the sixth hour ... the ninth hour
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the time as readers count it today.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: Readable uses the more familiar word.

decisions.choice: midi ... quinze heures (B); le milieu de la journée ... trois heures de l’après-midi (R)
alternatives: la sixième heure ... la neuvième heure at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:33: written French gives the afternoon hour on the 24-hour clock; Readable says it as people say it aloud. Literal keeps the ancient hours.

decisions.choice: le voile du sanctuaire (L, B); le grand rideau du temple (R); tout le pays at every level
decisions.reason: "Le voile" is the traditional French name for this curtain, as in Mark 15:38; Readable uses the everyday "rideau". "Tout le pays" keeps the reading of m2 (the land of Israel); "toute la terre" would suggest the whole world.

decisions.choice: saa sita, saa tisa at every level; mchana and alasiri added at Balanced and Readable
alternatives: saa tisa (the English "three in the afternoon")
decisions.reason: The Greek counts the hours from sunrise, as Swahili time does, so the sixth and ninth hours are "saa sita" and "saa tisa" with no conversion (meaning decision m1), as in Mark 15:33.

decisions.choice: "giờ thứ sáu ... giờ thứ chín" (L); "giữa trưa", "mười hai giờ trưa" ... "ba giờ chiều" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek count; Balanced and Readable give the modern time, as the style guide and the Vietnamese Mark 15:33 do.

decisions.choice: "đền thờ" for the sanctuary (naos)
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "đền thờ" for naos at every level; the curtain shows the temple building itself is meant (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "여섯째 시", "아홉째 시" (L); "낮 열두 시", "오후 세 시" (B, R)
alternatives: the Greek count at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek count, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (style guide, section 5), as the Korean Mark 15:33.

decisions.choice: "성소의 휘장" (L, B); "성전 안에 드리워져 있던 휘장" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean Mark 15:38 for the curtain of the sanctuary (meaning decision).

source.text: καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου.

records.literal_gloss: And having called out with a voice loud the Jesus said, Father, into hands of you I entrust the spirit of me.

en.L: And Jesus called out with a loud voice and said, "Father, into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands I entrust {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spirit."
en.B: Then Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Father, I place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spirit in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands."
en.R: Then Jesus shouted, "Father, I give {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spirit into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} care!"

es.L: Y Jesús, clamando con gran voz, dijo: «Padre, en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos confío {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espíritu».
es.B: Entonces Jesús clamó con fuerte voz: «Padre, pongo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espíritu en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos».
es.R: Entonces Jesús gritó: «¡Padre, dejo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espíritu a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} cuidado!».

fr.L: Et Jésus, ayant crié d’une voix forte, dit : « Père, entre {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains je remets {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esprit. »
fr.B: Alors Jésus poussa un grand cri : « Père, je remets {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esprit entre {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains. »
fr.R: Puis Jésus a crié : « Père, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} confie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esprit ! »

sw.L: Na Yesu, akiita kwa sauti kuu, alisema, "Baba, mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}} ninaweka amana roho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."
sw.B: Kisha Yesu alilia kwa sauti kubwa, "Baba, ninaitia roho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alipaza sauti, "Baba, ninaiweka roho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} chini ya ulinzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}!"

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu kêu lớn tiếng mà nói: "Lạy Cha, vào tay Cha, Con xin giao phó thần linh Con."
vi.B: Rồi Đức Giê-xu kêu lớn: "Lạy Cha, Con xin phó thác thần linh Con trong tay Cha."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu kêu lớn tiếng: "Lạy Cha, Con xin giao thần linh Con cho Cha gìn giữ!"

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 큰 소리로 외쳐 말씀하셨다. "아버지, 아버지의 손에 제 영을 맡깁니다."
ko.B: 예수께서 큰 소리로 외치셨다. "아버지, 제 영을 아버지의 손에 맡깁니다."
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서 큰 소리로 외치셨다. "아버지, 제 영을 아버지께 맡깁니다!"

decisions.choice: into your hands I entrust my spirit: the words of Psalm 31
decisions.reason: The prayer is Psalm 31:6, the prayer of one who trusts God when enemies surround him. Jesus adds "Father".

decisions.choice: entrust: hand over for safekeeping
decisions.reason: The verb is used for placing something in someone's care (12:48; Acts 20:32). Jesus dies trusting his Father.

decisions.choice: spirit: his life, his very self
decisions.reason: At death the spirit leaves the body (8:55). Stephen prays in the same way as he dies (Acts 7:59).

decisions.choice: a loud voice: a strong cry, not a faint whisper
decisions.reason: Mark 15:37 also tells of a loud cry at the moment of death.

decisions.choice: into your care
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: confío (L); pongo ... en tus manos (B); dejo ... a tu cuidado (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to hand something over for safekeeping (meaning decision m2). "Confiar" says this plainly in modern Spanish; Balanced and Readable follow the English. Jesus's "mi" takes the setting where the English "my" does.

decisions.choice: ninaweka amana (L); ninaitia ... mikononi mwako (B); ninaiweka ... chini ya ulinzi wako (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to hand something over for safekeeping (meaning decision m2). "Kuweka amana" is to deposit something in trust, which says exactly that at Literal; "kukabidhi" is kept for the handing over of Jesus to his enemies (23:25). Readable says "into your care", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Con" for Jesus' "my" and "Cha" for "your", with no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: In prayer Jesus calls himself "Con" and the Father "Cha" (as in John 17 and the Vietnamese Mark 15:34); these are nouns of address with no capital form for the setting.

decisions.choice: "thần linh" for spirit
decisions.reason: As in John 19:30, where Jesus gives up his spirit; the meaning decision reads it as his life, his very self.

decisions.choice: "아버지의 손에" (L, B), "아버지께" (R); "영" for pneuma
decisions.reason: Korean addresses the Father by title, not "당신"; Readable says "to you" without the picture of hands, as the English Readable does. "영" keeps the words of Psalm 31 (meaning decision).

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν.

records.literal_gloss: This then having said he breathed out.

en.L: And having said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} breathed out [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}} last].
en.B: With these words {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} breathed out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} last breath.
en.R: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died.

es.L: Y, habiendo dicho esto, expiró.
es.B: Dicho esto, expiró.
es.R: Después de decir esto, murió.

fr.L: Et ayant dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} expira.
fr.B: Sur ces mots, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rendit {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} dernier soupir.
fr.R: Après avoir dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort.

sw.L: Naye, akiisha kusema haya, alitoa pumzi [{{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}] ya mwisho.
sw.B: Baada ya kusema maneno hayo, alikata roho.
sw.R: Baada ya kusema hivyo, alikufa.

vi.L: Nói xong điều này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tắt thở.
vi.B: Nói xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trút hơi thở cuối cùng.
vi.R: Nói xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua đời.

ko.L: 그리고 이 말씀을 하시고 숨을 거두셨다.
ko.B: 이 말씀을 하시고 숨을 거두셨다.
ko.R: 이렇게 말씀하시고 예수께서는 돌아가셨다.

decisions.choice: breathed out: died
decisions.reason: The verb means to breathe out, a gentle way of saying that someone died (Mark 15:37). It is related to the word for spirit in the prayer just spoken.

decisions.choice: died
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: alitoa pumzi [yake] ya mwisho (L); alikata roho (B); alikufa (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to breathe out, to breathe one's last (meaning decision m1), the same verb as in Mark 15:37, so Swahili uses the same words: the last breath at Literal, the everyday idiom "kukata roho" at Balanced, and plainly "died" at Readable, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "숨을 거두다" (L, B); "돌아가시다" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean Mark 15:37.

source.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης τὸ γενόμενον ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεὸν λέγων· Ὄντως ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος ἦν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the centurion that having happened he was glorifying the God saying, Certainly the man this righteous was.

en.L: And when the centurion saw what had happened, he began glorifying God, saying, "Certainly this man was righteous."
en.B: The centurion saw what had taken place, and he gave glory to God, saying, "Truly this man was righteous."
en.R: The Roman army officer saw what had happened. He gave glory to God and said, "This man really was righteous. He had done nothing wrong!"

es.L: Y el centurión, al ver lo sucedido, glorificaba a Dios, diciendo: «Ciertamente este hombre era justo».
es.B: El centurión vio lo que había pasado y dio gloria a Dios, diciendo: «Verdaderamente este hombre era justo».
es.R: El oficial del ejército romano vio lo que había pasado. Dio gloria a Dios y dijo: «De verdad este hombre era justo. ¡No había hecho nada malo!».

fr.L: Et le centurion, voyant ce qui était arrivé, glorifiait Dieu, disant : « Vraiment, cet homme était juste. »
fr.B: Voyant ce qui s’était passé, le centurion rendit gloire à Dieu en disant : « Vraiment, cet homme était juste ! »
fr.R: Un officier de l’armée romaine a vu ce qui était arrivé. Il a rendu gloire à Dieu et il a dit : « Cet homme était vraiment juste. Il n’avait rien fait de mal ! »

sw.L: Naye akida, alipoona yaliyotukia, alikuwa akimtukuza Mungu, akisema, "Hakika mtu huyu alikuwa mwenye haki."
sw.B: Akida alipoona yaliyotokea, alimpa Mungu utukufu, akisema, "Kweli mtu huyu alikuwa mwenye haki."
sw.R: Afisa wa jeshi la Kirumi aliona yaliyotokea. Akamtukuza Mungu, akasema, "Kweli mtu huyu alikuwa mwenye haki. Hakuwa amefanya kosa lolote!"

vi.L: Viên đội trưởng thấy việc đã xảy ra thì tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời mà nói: "Thật, người này đã là người công chính."
vi.B: Viên đội trưởng thấy những gì đã xảy ra thì tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời và nói: "Người này thật là người công chính!"
vi.R: Một sĩ quan La Mã thấy những gì đã xảy ra. Ông tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời và nói: "Người này thật là người công chính. Ông ấy không làm điều gì sai cả!"

ko.L: 그런데 백부장이 일어난 일을 보고 하나님께 영광을 돌리며 말했다. "참으로 이 사람은 의인이었다."
ko.B: 백부장은 일어난 일을 보고 하나님께 영광을 돌리며 말했다. "이분은 참으로 의로운 분이셨다."
ko.R: 로마 군대의 장교가 이 일을 보고 하나님께 영광을 돌리며 말했다. "이분은 정말 의로운 분이셨다. 아무 잘못도 하지 않으셨다!"

decisions.choice: the centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: Centurions commanded the soldiers who carried out executions. Luke speaks well of other centurions (7:2-9; Acts 10:1-2).

decisions.choice: righteous: both innocent of the charge and right before God
alternatives: righteous only, in a religious sense
decisions.reason: The word means just or righteous. After Pilate's verdicts and the criminal's words (23:4, 14, 22, 41), it surely includes "innocent". But Luke uses the same word for people who are right with God (1:6; 2:25; 23:50), and in Acts Jesus is called "the Righteous One" (Acts 3:14; 7:52; 22:14), recalling the righteous servant of Isaiah 53:11. Where Mark 15:39 and Matthew 27:54 have "Son of God", Luke gives this word.

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praise even at Jesus' death
decisions.reason: In Luke people often glorify God when they see what Jesus does (5:25; 7:16; 13:13; 18:43). Here a Gentile soldier does so when he sees how Jesus died.

decisions.choice: he began glorifying: the imperfect tense
decisions.reason: The tense describes an action begun and continued.

decisions.choice: gave glory to God
decisions.reason: The key term is kept with the noun "glory", which reads more naturally than "glorified".

decisions.choice: He had done nothing wrong!
decisions.reason: Readable adds the sense of innocence that the word carries in this setting, as the criminal said in 23:41.

decisions.choice: The Roman army officer
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a centurion was.

decisions.choice: centurión (L, B), oficial del ejército romano (R); justo (every level)
decisions.reason: The officer over about a hundred soldiers (meaning decision m1), named as in Matthew 27 and Mark 15. "Justo" is the word of the key term "justicia" and keeps both senses, innocent and right before God (meaning decision m2, uncertain); Readable adds what the English adds.

decisions.choice: le centurion (L, B); un officier de l’armée romaine (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament term sheet: "centurion" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what he was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: akida (L, B), afisa wa jeshi la Kirumi (R); mwenye haki (every level)
decisions.reason: The officer over about a hundred soldiers (meaning decision m1), named as in Matthew 27 and Mark 15. "Mwenye haki" carries the key term "haki" and keeps both senses, innocent and right before God (meaning decision m2, uncertain); Readable adds what the English adds.

decisions.choice: "viên đội trưởng" (L, B); "một sĩ quan La Mã" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:39.

decisions.choice: "người công chính" at every level
decisions.reason: The key term "công chính" keeps both senses the meaning decision gives, innocent of the charge and right before God; Readable adds the first sense in a second sentence, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "이 사람은 ... 의인이었다" (L); "이분은 ... 의로운 분이셨다" (B, R); "백부장" (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 15:39: Literal keeps "this man", and in Balanced and Readable the centurion's verdict would sound grudging without the honorific. "의" is the key term for righteous.

source.text: καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαραγενόμενοι ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν ταύτην, θεωρήσαντες τὰ γενόμενα, τύπτοντες τὰ στήθη ὑπέστρεφον.

records.literal_gloss: And all the having come together crowds to the spectacle this, having seen the things having happened, beating the breasts were returning.

en.L: And all the crowds who had come together for this spectacle, having seen the things that had happened, were returning, beating [their] breasts.
en.B: All the crowds who had gathered to watch this spectacle saw what had happened, and they turned back home, striking their breasts.
en.R: Large crowds had come to watch. When they saw what happened, they beat their chests in sorrow as they went home.

es.L: Y todas las multitudes que se habían reunido para este espectáculo, al ver lo sucedido, se volvían golpeándose los pechos.
es.B: Todas las multitudes que se habían reunido para presenciar aquel espectáculo vieron lo que había pasado y regresaron a sus casas golpeándose el pecho.
es.R: Mucha gente había venido a mirar. Cuando vieron lo que pasó, se golpeaban el pecho de tristeza mientras volvían a sus casas.

fr.L: Et toutes les foules qui s’étaient rassemblées pour ce spectacle, ayant vu ce qui était arrivé, s’en retournaient en se frappant la poitrine.
fr.B: Toutes les foules venues assister à ce spectacle virent ce qui était arrivé, et elles s’en retournèrent chez elles en se frappant la poitrine.
fr.R: Une grande foule était venue regarder. Quand les gens ont vu ce qui s’était passé, ils sont rentrés chez eux en se frappant la poitrine de tristesse.

sw.L: Na makundi yote ya watu waliokuwa wamekusanyika pamoja kwa ajili ya tamasha hili, walipoyaona yaliyotukia, walirudi wakijipiga vifua.
sw.B: Watu wote waliokusanyika kutazama tukio hilo waliona yaliyotokea, wakarudi nyumbani wakijipiga vifua.
sw.R: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulikuwa umekuja kutazama. Walipoona yaliyotokea, walijipiga vifua kwa huzuni walipokuwa wakirudi nyumbani.

vi.L: Và tất cả các đám đông đã tụ họp lại để xem cảnh tượng này, khi thấy những việc đã xảy ra, thì đấm ngực mà trở về.
vi.B: Tất cả đám đông kéo đến xem cảnh tượng ấy, khi thấy những việc đã xảy ra, đều đấm ngực mà trở về nhà.
vi.R: Có rất nhiều người đã kéo đến xem. Khi thấy những việc đã xảy ra, họ đấm ngực tỏ lòng buồn rầu rồi đi về nhà.

ko.L: 그리고 이 구경거리를 보려고 함께 모여든 모든 무리가 일어난 일들을 보고, 가슴을 치며 돌아갔다.
ko.B: 이 광경을 보려고 모여든 무리도 모두 일어난 일을 보고 가슴을 치며 돌아갔다.
ko.R: 많은 사람이 이 일을 구경하러 와 있었다. 그들은 일어난 일을 보고 슬퍼서 가슴을 치며 집으로 돌아갔다.

decisions.choice: beating their breasts: a sign of grief and sorrow for sin
decisions.reason: The tax collector in the temple beat his breast as he prayed for mercy (18:13). The crowds who came to watch go home grieving.

decisions.choice: spectacle: a public sight that people come to watch
decisions.reason: The word is used for a show or public event. The crowds came to look, as at an execution, and went away changed.

decisions.choice: the crowds' grief: a first turning
decisions.reason: The people who had been gathered against Jesus now mourn. In Acts many in Jerusalem are cut to the heart when they hear what they have done (Acts 2:37).

decisions.choice: in sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant.

source.text: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ πάντες οἱ γνωστοὶ αὐτῷ μακρόθεν, καὶ γυναῖκες αἱ συνακολουθοῦσαι αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὁρῶσαι ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: Stood then all the knowing him from afar, and women the having followed with him from the Galilee, seeing these things.

en.L: And all those who knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} stood at a distance, and [the] women who had followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee, seeing these things.
en.B: Everyone who knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} stood far off. The women who had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee were standing there too, and they saw these things.
en.R: All of Jesus' friends were standing far away. The women who had followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee were there too. They watched everything that happened.

es.L: Y todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocían estaban de pie a lo lejos, y [las] mujeres que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían acompañado desde Galilea, mirando estas cosas.
es.B: Todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocían se quedaron lejos. También estaban allí las mujeres que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían acompañado desde Galilea, y vieron estas cosas.
es.R: Todos los amigos de Jesús estaban lejos. Las mujeres que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían seguido desde Galilea también estaban allí. Miraban todo lo que pasaba.

fr.L: Et tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissaient se tenaient à distance, ainsi que les femmes qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient accompagné depuis la Galilée, regardant ces choses.
fr.B: Tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissaient se tenaient au loin. Les femmes qui étaient venues de Galilée avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} étaient là aussi, et elles virent ces choses.
fr.R: Tous les amis de Jésus se tenaient loin. Les femmes qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient suivi depuis la Galilée étaient là, elles aussi. Elles ont regardé tout ce qui se passait.

sw.L: Na wote waliomjua walikuwa wamesimama kwa mbali, na wanawake waliofuatana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kutoka Galilaya, wakiyaona mambo haya.
sw.B: Wote waliomfahamu walisimama mbali. Wanawake waliokuja pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kutoka Galilaya walikuwa pale pia, wakayaona mambo hayo.
sw.R: Marafiki wote wa Yesu walikuwa wamesimama mbali. Wanawake waliomfuata kutoka Galilaya walikuwa pale pia. Waliona kila kitu kilichotukia.

vi.L: Còn tất cả những người quen biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đều đứng ở xa, cùng những người phụ nữ đã theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Ga-li-lê, nhìn xem những việc này.
vi.B: Tất cả những người quen biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đều đứng đằng xa. Những người phụ nữ đã theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Ga-li-lê cũng đứng đó và nhìn thấy những việc này.
vi.R: Tất cả bạn bè của Đức Giê-xu đứng ở đằng xa. Những người phụ nữ đã theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Ga-li-lê cũng ở đó. Họ nhìn thấy mọi việc đã xảy ra.

ko.L: 그리고 그분을 아는 모든 사람이 멀리 서 있었고, 갈릴리에서부터 그분을 따라온 여자들도 이 일들을 보고 있었다.
ko.B: 예수를 아는 사람들은 모두 멀리 서 있었다. 갈릴리에서부터 예수를 따라온 여자들도 거기 서서 이 일들을 지켜보았다.
ko.R: 예수의 친구들은 모두 멀리 떨어져 서 있었다. 갈릴리에서부터 예수를 따라온 여자들도 거기 있었다. 그들은 이 모든 일을 지켜보았다.

decisions.choice: standing at a distance: the friends of the sufferer
alternatives: a detail of no further meaning
decisions.reason: Psalm 38:12 speaks of the sufferer's friends and neighbors who stand far off.

decisions.choice: those who knew him: his friends and acquaintances
decisions.reason: The word means people known to someone. It may include the apostles and other disciples.

decisions.choice: seeing: the women are the ones who saw
decisions.reason: The participle is feminine. Luke stresses that the women saw what happened; they will see the burial (23:55) and find the tomb empty (24:1-10).

decisions.choice: the women from Galilee: those who had followed and supported Jesus
decisions.reason: Luke has named some of them: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many others (8:2-3; 24:10).

decisions.choice: Jesus' friends
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for those who knew him.

source.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων, ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συγκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὃς προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι, καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν οὐδεὶς οὔπω κείμενος.

records.literal_gloss: And behold a man by name Joseph a council member being, a man good and righteous \v 51 this [one] not was having agreed to the plan and the action of them from Arimathea a city of the Jews, who was waiting for the kingdom of the God, \v 52 this [one] having gone to the Pilate asked [for] the body of the Jesus, \v 53 and having taken down he wrapped it in linen cloth, and placed him in a tomb cut in rock where not was no one not yet lying.

en.L: And look, [there was] a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man \v 51 (he had not agreed with their plan and action), from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who was waiting for the kingdom of God. \v 52 This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus, \v 53 and having taken [it] down, he wrapped it in a linen cloth and placed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb cut in rock, where no one had ever yet been laid.
en.B: There was a man named Joseph who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man \v 51 who had not given his consent to what the council planned and did. He came from Arimathea, a town of the Jews, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God. \v 52 He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. \v 53 He took the body down from the cross and wrapped it in a linen sheet. Then he laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb cut out of the rock, where no one had ever been buried.
en.R: There was a man named Joseph. He was a member of the Jewish council. He was a good man who did what was right in God's eyes. \v 51 He had not agreed with the plan of the other leaders or with what they had done. He came from Arimathea, a Jewish town, and he was waiting for God to set up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom. \v 52 Joseph went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. \v 53 He took the body down from the cross and wrapped it in a linen cloth. Then he laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb that had been cut out of rock. No one had ever been buried in it before.

es.L: Y mira, [había] un hombre llamado José, que era miembro del concilio, hombre bueno y justo \v 51 (este no había dado su consentimiento al plan ni a la acción de ellos), de Arimatea, ciudad de los judíos, que esperaba el reino de Dios. \v 52 Este fue a Pilato y pidió el cuerpo de Jesús, \v 53 y, después de bajar[lo], lo envolvió en una sábana de lino y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso en un sepulcro excavado en la roca, donde nadie había sido puesto todavía.
es.B: Había un hombre llamado José, miembro del Consejo, hombre bueno y justo, \v 51 que no había dado su consentimiento a lo que el Consejo había planeado y hecho. Era de Arimatea, un pueblo de los judíos, y esperaba el reino de Dios. \v 52 Fue a ver a Pilato y le pidió el cuerpo de Jesús. \v 53 Bajó el cuerpo de la cruz y lo envolvió en una sábana de lino. Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso en un sepulcro excavado en la roca, donde nadie había sido sepultado todavía.
es.R: Había un hombre llamado José. Era miembro del Consejo Supremo de los judíos. Era un hombre bueno, que hacía lo que era justo a los ojos de Dios. \v 51 No había estado de acuerdo con el plan de los otros líderes ni con lo que habían hecho. Era de Arimatea, un pueblo judío, y esperaba que Dios estableciera {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino. \v 52 José fue a ver a Pilato y le pidió el cuerpo de Jesús. \v 53 Bajó el cuerpo de la cruz y lo envolvió en una tela de lino. Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso en una tumba que había sido excavada en la roca. Nadie había sido sepultado allí antes.

fr.L: Et voici un homme du nom de Joseph, qui était membre du conseil, homme bon et juste \v 51 (il n’avait pas donné son accord à leur décision et à leur action), d’Arimathée, ville des Juifs, qui attendait le royaume de Dieu. \v 52 Cet homme alla trouver Pilate et demanda le corps de Jésus, \v 53 et, l’ayant descendu, il l’enveloppa dans un drap de lin et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} déposa dans un tombeau taillé dans le roc, où personne n’avait encore été déposé.
fr.B: Il y avait un homme nommé Joseph, membre du Sanhédrin, homme bon et juste, \v 51 qui n’avait pas donné son accord à ce que le conseil avait projeté et fait. Il était d’Arimathée, une ville des Juifs, et il attendait le royaume de Dieu. \v 52 Il alla trouver Pilate et demanda le corps de Jésus. \v 53 Il descendit le corps de la croix et l’enveloppa dans un drap de lin. Puis il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} déposa dans un tombeau taillé dans le roc, où personne n’avait encore été enseveli.
fr.R: Il y avait un homme appelé Joseph. Il était membre du grand conseil des Juifs. C’était un homme bon, qui faisait ce qui est juste aux yeux de Dieu. \v 51 Il n’avait pas été d’accord avec le projet des autres chefs, ni avec ce qu’ils avaient fait. Il venait d’Arimathée, une ville juive, et il attendait que Dieu établisse {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume. \v 52 Joseph est allé voir Pilate et lui a demandé le corps de Jésus. \v 53 Il a descendu le corps de la croix et l’a enveloppé dans un drap de lin. Puis il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a déposé dans un tombeau qui avait été creusé dans le rocher. Personne n’y avait encore jamais été enterré.

sw.L: Na tazama, mtu mmoja aitwaye Yusufu, aliyekuwa mjumbe wa baraza, mtu mwema na mwenye haki \v 51 (huyu hakuwa ameunga mkono mpango na kitendo chao), wa Arimathaya, mji wa Wayahudi, ambaye alikuwa akiutazamia ufalme wa Mungu. \v 52 Huyu alimwendea Pilato, akaomba mwili wa Yesu, \v 53 na akiisha kuushusha, aliufunga kwa sanda ya kitani, akamlaza katika kaburi lililochongwa mwambani, ambamo hakuna mtu aliyekuwa amewahi kulazwa bado.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na mtu mmoja aitwaye Yusufu, mjumbe wa baraza, mtu mwema na mwenye haki, \v 51 ambaye hakuwa amekubali yale ambayo baraza lilipanga na kutenda. Alikuwa wa Arimathaya, mji wa Wayahudi, naye alikuwa akiungojea ufalme wa Mungu. \v 52 Alimwendea Pilato, akaomba apewe mwili wa Yesu. \v 53 Akaushusha mwili kutoka msalabani, akaufunga kwa shuka la kitani. Kisha akamlaza katika kaburi lililochongwa katika mwamba, ambamo hakuna mtu aliyekuwa amewahi kuzikwa.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na mtu mmoja aitwaye Yusufu. Alikuwa mjumbe wa baraza kuu la Wayahudi. Alikuwa mtu mwema aliyefanya yaliyo haki machoni pa Mungu. \v 51 Hakuwa amekubaliana na mpango wa viongozi wengine wala na yale waliyoyafanya. Alitoka Arimathaya, mji wa Wayahudi, naye alikuwa akingojea Mungu aanzishe ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. \v 52 Yusufu alikwenda kwa Pilato, akaomba mwili wa Yesu. \v 53 Akaushusha mwili kutoka msalabani, akaufunga kwa kitambaa cha kitani. Kisha akamlaza katika kaburi lililokuwa limechongwa katika mwamba. Hakuna mtu aliyekuwa amewahi kuzikwa humo kabla.

vi.L: Và kìa, có một người tên là Giô-sép, là một nghị viên, một người tốt lành và công chính \v 51 (người này đã không đồng ý với mưu định và việc làm của họ), [quê] ở A-ri-ma-thê, một thành của người Do Thái, là người trông đợi vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 52 Người này đến gặp Phi-lát và xin thi thể của Đức Giê-xu, \v 53 rồi hạ [thi thể] xuống, ông quấn thi thể trong vải gai, và đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong một ngôi mộ đục trong đá, là nơi chưa từng có ai được đặt vào.
vi.B: Có một người tên là Giô-sép, thành viên của Hội đồng Công luận, một người tốt lành và công chính. \v 51 Ông đã không đồng ý với những gì hội đồng đã bàn định và thực hiện. Ông quê ở A-ri-ma-thê, một thành của người Do Thái, và ông đang trông đợi vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 52 Ông đến gặp Phi-lát và xin thi thể của Đức Giê-xu. \v 53 Ông hạ thi thể xuống khỏi cây thập tự, lấy một tấm vải gai quấn lại, rồi đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào một ngôi mộ đục trong đá, nơi chưa hề có ai được chôn.
vi.R: Có một người tên là Giô-sép. Ông là một thành viên của hội đồng tối cao của người Do Thái. Ông là người tốt, sống ngay thẳng trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời. \v 51 Ông đã không đồng ý với kế hoạch và việc làm của các nhà lãnh đạo khác. Ông quê ở A-ri-ma-thê, một thị trấn của người Do Thái, và ông đang trông đợi Đức Chúa Trời thiết lập vương quốc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 52 Giô-sép đến gặp Phi-lát và xin thi thể của Đức Giê-xu. \v 53 Ông hạ thi thể xuống khỏi cây thập tự và quấn trong một tấm vải gai. Rồi ông đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào một ngôi mộ được đục trong vách đá. Chưa có ai được chôn trong mộ ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 보라, 요셉이라는 이름의 사람이 있었는데, 그는 공의회 의원이었고 선하고 의로운 사람이었다. \v 51 (이 사람은 그들의 결정과 행동에 동의하지 않았다.) 그는 유대인의 도시 아리마대 출신이었고, 하나님의 나라를 기다리고 있었다. \v 52 이 사람이 빌라도에게 가서 예수의 시신을 달라고 요청했다. \v 53 그리고 [시신을] 내려 고운 베로 싸고, 바위를 깎아 만든 무덤, 아직 아무도 놓인 적이 없는 [무덤]에 그분을 모셨다.
ko.B: 요셉이라는 사람이 있었다. 그는 공의회 의원이었고, 선하고 의로운 사람이었다. \v 51 그는 공의회의 결정과 행동에 찬성하지 않았다. 그는 유대인의 마을 아리마대 출신으로, 하나님의 나라를 기다리고 있었다. \v 52 그가 빌라도에게 가서 예수의 시신을 내어 달라고 청했다. \v 53 그리고 시신을 십자가에서 내려 고운 베로 감싸고, 바위를 파서 만든 무덤에 예수를 모셨다. 그 무덤에는 아직 아무도 묻힌 적이 없었다.
ko.R: 요셉이라는 사람이 있었다. 그는 유대 최고 의회의 의원이었다. 그는 선한 사람이었고, 하나님 보시기에 옳은 일을 하는 사람이었다. \v 51 그는 다른 지도자들의 계획에도, 그들이 한 일에도 찬성하지 않았다. 그는 유대인의 마을 아리마대에서 왔다. 그리고 하나님께서 그분의 나라를 세우시기를 기다리고 있었다. \v 52 요셉은 빌라도에게 가서 예수의 시신을 달라고 부탁했다. \v 53 그리고 시신을 십자가에서 내려 고운 베 천으로 감쌌다. 그다음에 바위를 파서 만든 무덤에 예수를 모셨다. 그 무덤에는 전에 아무도 묻힌 적이 없었다.

decisions.choice: a member of the council: one of the leaders who made up the Jewish council
decisions.reason: The council had condemned Jesus and brought him to Pilate (22:66-23:1). Mark 15:43 calls Joseph a respected member of it.

decisions.choice: righteous: right with God and faithful to his law
decisions.reason: The same word as in 23:47. Luke uses it for Zechariah and Elizabeth (1:6) and Simeon (2:25).

decisions.choice: a remark in the middle of the sentence: he had not agreed
decisions.reason: The clause interrupts the description of Joseph; Literal marks it with parentheses.

decisions.choice: Arimathea: a town of Judea
decisions.reason: Its location is not certain. It is often taken to be Ramathaim, the hometown of Samuel (1 Samuel 1:1).

decisions.choice: waiting for the kingdom of God: like the faithful at the start of the Gospel
decisions.reason: Simeon waited for the comfort of Israel and Anna spoke to all who waited for the redemption of Jerusalem (2:25, 38). Joseph shares that hope.

decisions.choice: it ... him: the body, then Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Joseph wraps "it", the body, but lays "him" in the tomb; the second pronoun is masculine and refers to Jesus.

decisions.choice: a linen cloth and a rock-cut tomb where no one had been laid
decisions.reason: Bodies were wrapped in linen and laid in tombs cut into rock. The law said a hanged man's body must not be left overnight (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). A new tomb was fitting for a king; Jesus had entered Jerusalem on a colt no one had ever ridden (19:30).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to introduce a new person. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: from the cross
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the body was taken down from.

decisions.choice: a good man who did what was right in God's eyes
decisions.reason: Readable explains what righteous means here.

decisions.choice: lo envolvió (plain) ... {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso
decisions.reason: The first pronoun means the body, the second Jesus himself (meaning decision m6), so only the second takes the setting, as in the English, where "it" and "him" differ.

decisions.choice: sepulcro (L, B); tumba (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, as in Mark 15:46, recorded once in this chapter: "sepulcro" at Literal and Balanced, the everyday "tumba" at Readable. The same in 23:55.

decisions.choice: membre du conseil (L); membre du Sanhédrin (B); membre du grand conseil des Juifs (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names a member of the council; Balanced and Readable use the term sheet's names for the Jewish council, as Mark 15:43 does, and Literal keeps the plain word, which also matches "their plan" in 23:51.

decisions.choice: l’enveloppa (the body) ... le déposa (Jesus), with the setting only on the second
decisions.reason: As the meaning decision says (m6), the Greek moves from "it", the body, to "him", Jesus; French "corps" is masculine, so both pronouns are masculine, and the setting marks only the one for Jesus himself, as the English does.

decisions.choice: aliufunga (-u-, the body) ... akamlaza (-m-, Jesus)
decisions.reason: Luke says "it" of the body and "him" of Jesus himself (meaning decision m6). Swahili shows the same shift in the object prefix: -u- for "mwili" (body), -m- for a person. Neither prefix can take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "một nghị viên" (L); "thành viên của Hội đồng Công luận" (B); "hội đồng tối cao của người Do Thái" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:43: Literal keeps the single Greek word, Balanced and Readable name the council.

decisions.choice: "quấn thi thể ... đặt Ngài" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Luke's change from "it" (the body) to "him" (meaning decision); Vietnamese has no neuter pronoun, so it names the body.

decisions.choice: "공의회 의원" (L, B), "유대 최고 의회의 의원" (R); "시신"; "고운 베" (L, B), "고운 베 천" (R); "모시다" for laying Jesus in the tomb
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean Mark 15:43-46 and John 19:38-42; "시신" is the respectful word. Literal keeps the shift from the body ("[시신을]") to Jesus himself ("그분을"), as the meaning decision notes.

source.text: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν παρασκευῆς, καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν.

records.literal_gloss: And day it was of preparation, and Sabbath was dawning.

en.L: And it was [the] day of Preparation, and [the] Sabbath was beginning to dawn.
en.B: It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near.
en.R: It was Friday, the day when people got ready for the Sabbath. The Sabbath would begin at sunset.

es.L: Y era [el] día de la Preparación, y [el] sábado comenzaba a amanecer.
es.B: Era el día de la Preparación, y el sábado estaba a punto de comenzar.
es.R: Era viernes, el día en que la gente se preparaba para el sábado. El sábado comenzaría al ponerse el sol.

fr.L: Et c’était le jour de la Préparation, et le sabbat commençait à poindre.
fr.B: C’était le jour de la Préparation, et le sabbat approchait.
fr.R: C’était vendredi, le jour où l’on préparait tout pour le sabbat. Le sabbat allait commencer au coucher du soleil.

sw.L: Na ilikuwa siku ya Maandalio, na Sabato ilikuwa ikianza kupambazuka.
sw.B: Ilikuwa siku ya Maandalio, na Sabato ilikuwa inakaribia.
sw.R: Ilikuwa Ijumaa, siku ambayo watu walijiandaa kwa ajili ya Sabato. Sabato ingeanza jua litakapozama.

vi.L: Và hôm ấy là ngày Chuẩn Bị, và [ngày] Sa-bát đang rạng đến.
vi.B: Hôm ấy là ngày Chuẩn Bị, và ngày Sa-bát sắp bắt đầu.
vi.R: Hôm ấy là Thứ Sáu, ngày người ta chuẩn bị cho ngày Sa-bát. Ngày Sa-bát sẽ bắt đầu lúc mặt trời lặn.

ko.L: 그날은 준비일이었고, 안식일이 밝아 오고 있었다.
ko.B: 그날은 준비일이었고, 안식일이 다가오고 있었다.
ko.R: 그날은 금요일, 곧 안식일을 준비하는 날이었다. 해가 지면 안식일이 시작될 참이었다.

decisions.choice: the day of Preparation: Friday, the day before the Sabbath
decisions.reason: On Friday people prepared food and everything else they needed, since no work could be done on the Sabbath (Mark 15:42).

decisions.choice: dawning: beginning
decisions.reason: The verb is used for daybreak, but the Sabbath began at sunset on Friday. It may refer to the evening star or the lamps lit as the Sabbath began, or simply mean that it was beginning.

decisions.choice: Friday ... at sunset
decisions.reason: Readable names the day and says when the Sabbath began.

decisions.choice: comenzaba a amanecer (L); estaba a punto de comenzar (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is to dawn, used here for a day beginning (meaning decision m2); the Sabbath began at sunset. Literal keeps the picture, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what is meant.

decisions.choice: ikianza kupambazuka (L); inakaribia (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is to dawn, used here for a day beginning (meaning decision m2); the Sabbath began at sunset. Literal keeps the picture, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what is meant.

decisions.choice: "ngày Chuẩn Bị" (L, B), "Thứ Sáu" (R); "đang rạng đến" (L), "sắp bắt đầu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "ngày Chuẩn Bị" as in the Vietnamese Mark 15:42; Readable names the weekday, as the English Readable does. Literal keeps the Greek word for dawning, though the Sabbath began at sunset (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "준비일" (L, B), "안식일을 준비하는 날" (R); "밝아 오다" (L), "다가오다" (B)
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean Mark 15:42. Literal keeps the Greek picture of dawning, though the Sabbath began at sunset (meaning decision).

source.text: κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ αἱ γυναῖκες, αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ, ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ, ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα.

records.literal_gloss: Having followed after then the women, who were having come with out of the Galilee with him, saw the tomb and how was laid the body of him, \v 56 having returned then they prepared spices and perfumed oils.

en.L: And the women who had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of Galilee followed after and saw the tomb and how {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body was laid, \v 56 and having returned, they prepared spices and perfumed oils.
en.B: The women who had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee went after Joseph. They saw the tomb and the way {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body was laid there. \v 56 Then they went back and got spices and fragrant oils ready.
en.R: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph. They saw the tomb and how Jesus' body was placed in it. \v 56 Then they went home and made sweet-smelling spices and oils to put on the body.

es.L: Y las mujeres que habían venido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} desde Galilea siguieron detrás y vieron el sepulcro y cómo fue puesto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo, \v 56 y, al regresar, prepararon especias aromáticas y perfumes.
es.B: Las mujeres que habían venido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} desde Galilea siguieron a José. Vieron el sepulcro y la manera en que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo fue colocado allí. \v 56 Luego volvieron y prepararon especias y aceites perfumados.
es.R: Las mujeres que habían venido con Jesús desde Galilea siguieron a José. Vieron la tumba y cómo pusieron allí el cuerpo de Jesús. \v 56 Después se fueron a casa y prepararon especias y aceites de olor agradable para ponerlos en el cuerpo.

fr.L: Et les femmes qui étaient venues avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de la Galilée suivirent et virent le tombeau et comment {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps fut déposé, \v 56 et, s’en étant retournées, elles préparèrent des aromates et des huiles parfumées.
fr.B: Les femmes qui étaient venues de Galilée avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} suivirent Joseph. Elles virent le tombeau et la manière dont {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps y avait été placé. \v 56 Puis elles s’en retournèrent et préparèrent des aromates et des huiles parfumées.
fr.R: Les femmes qui étaient venues de Galilée avec Jésus ont suivi Joseph. Elles ont vu le tombeau et comment le corps de Jésus y avait été placé. \v 56 Ensuite, elles sont rentrées chez elles et elles ont préparé des épices et des huiles qui sentent bon, pour les mettre sur le corps.

sw.L: Na wale wanawake waliokuwa wamekuja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kutoka Galilaya walifuata nyuma, wakaliona kaburi na jinsi mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulivyowekwa, \v 56 na waliporudi, waliandaa manukato na mafuta yenye harufu nzuri.
sw.B: Wanawake waliokuja pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kutoka Galilaya walimfuata Yusufu. Waliliona kaburi na jinsi mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulivyolazwa humo. \v 56 Kisha wakarudi, wakaandaa manukato na mafuta mazuri.
sw.R: Wanawake waliokuja pamoja na Yesu kutoka Galilaya walimfuata Yusufu. Waliliona kaburi na jinsi mwili wa Yesu ulivyowekwa ndani yake. \v 56 Kisha walirudi nyumbani, wakatengeneza manukato na mafuta yenye harufu nzuri ya kupaka mwili.

vi.L: Còn những người phụ nữ đã cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Ga-li-lê đến thì đi theo sau, nhìn thấy ngôi mộ và thi thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được đặt [thế nào], \v 56 rồi trở về, họ chuẩn bị hương liệu và dầu thơm.
vi.B: Những người phụ nữ đã cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Ga-li-lê đến thì đi theo Giô-sép. Họ thấy ngôi mộ và thấy thi thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được đặt vào đó thế nào. \v 56 Rồi họ trở về và chuẩn bị hương liệu và dầu thơm.
vi.R: Những người phụ nữ đã đi với Đức Giê-xu từ Ga-li-lê đi theo Giô-sép. Họ thấy ngôi mộ và thấy người ta đặt thi thể Đức Giê-xu vào đó như thế nào. \v 56 Rồi họ về nhà và chuẩn bị hương liệu và dầu thơm để xức lên thi thể.

ko.L: 그리고 갈릴리에서 그분과 함께 온 여자들이 뒤따라가서, 무덤과 그분의 시신이 어떻게 놓였는지를 보았다. \v 56 그리고 돌아가서 향료와 향유를 준비했다.
ko.B: 갈릴리에서부터 예수와 함께 온 여자들이 요셉의 뒤를 따라가서, 무덤과 예수의 시신이 어떻게 놓였는지를 보았다. \v 56 그리고 돌아가서 향료와 향유를 마련했다.
ko.R: 갈릴리에서부터 예수와 함께 온 여자들이 요셉을 따라갔다. 그들은 무덤을 보았고, 예수의 시신이 어떻게 놓였는지도 보았다. \v 56 그러고 나서 집으로 돌아가, 시신에 바를 향료와 향유를 준비했다.

decisions.choice: they saw the tomb: the women are witnesses
decisions.reason: The women saw Jesus die (23:49), saw where and how he was laid, and two days later found the same tomb empty (24:1-3).

decisions.choice: spices and perfumed oils: for the body
decisions.reason: Spices and fragrant oils were put on a body as a last act of love and honor. The women brought them to the tomb on the first day of the week (24:1).

decisions.choice: went after Joseph (B); followed Joseph (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom they followed.

decisions.choice: to put on the body
decisions.reason: Readable says what the spices were for, as 24:1 shows.

decisions.choice: "hương liệu và dầu thơm"
decisions.reason: Spices and perfumed oils for the body (meaning decision); "hương liệu" as in the Vietnamese Mark 16:1.

decisions.choice: "향료" for aromata, "향유" for myra
decisions.reason: "향료" is the word of the Korean Mark 16:1 and John 19:40; "향유" is the ordinary word for perfumed oil.

source.text: Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν,

records.literal_gloss: And the indeed Sabbath they rested according to the commandment,

en.L: And on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
en.B: On the Sabbath they rested, as the commandment required.
en.R: On the Sabbath day they rested, as God's law said they must.

es.L: Y durante el sábado descansaron según el mandamiento.
es.B: El sábado descansaron, como lo exigía el mandamiento.
es.R: El día sábado descansaron, porque la ley de Dios decía que debían hacerlo.

fr.L: Et le sabbat, elles se reposèrent selon le commandement.
fr.B: Le jour du sabbat, elles se reposèrent, comme le commandement l’exigeait.
fr.R: Le jour du sabbat, elles se sont reposées, comme la Loi de Dieu l’ordonnait.

sw.L: Na siku ya Sabato walipumzika kwa kufuata amri.
sw.B: Siku ya Sabato walipumzika, kama amri ilivyotaka.
sw.R: Siku ya Sabato walipumzika, kwa sababu sheria ya Mungu ilisema ni lazima wapumzike.

vi.L: Và trong ngày Sa-bát, họ nghỉ ngơi theo điều răn.
vi.B: Trong ngày Sa-bát, họ nghỉ ngơi theo như điều răn dạy.
vi.R: Vào ngày Sa-bát, họ nghỉ ngơi, vì luật của Đức Chúa Trời đòi hỏi như vậy.

ko.L: 그리고 안식일에는 계명에 따라 쉬었다.
ko.B: 그리고 안식일에는 계명대로 쉬었다.
ko.R: 안식일에는 하나님의 율법이 정한 대로 쉬었다.

decisions.choice: the commandment: the law of the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The law commanded rest on the seventh day (Exodus 20:8-10; Deuteronomy 5:12-14). The women kept it before going to the tomb.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into 24:1
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends this verse with a comma: "on the Sabbath they rested ... but on the first day of the week" (24:1). Every level ends the sentence here, because a new chapter begins.

decisions.choice: God's law said they must
decisions.reason: Readable says whose commandment it was.
